description:
Wednesday AA Open Discussion Meeting 6PM PST 


AA members to share experience strength and home. Leader picks a topic related to alcohol then shares and opens the meeting for discussion about the topic.  Every Wednesday at 6pm, we are a small back County group. 

Verification is required.  
We are trying to keep our meeting safe.  
Please email early at least 15 to 20 minutes before the meeting starts.  We ask for your patience.

Please make sure you mention in your email which meeting Passcode you are requesting as well as sending us your phone number for a return call for verification.  We will call back before the next meeting and give you the password verbally. 

Please make sure your first name appears in your video when you log on and contact the secretary/host via chat when you arrive to let him know you received password via phone from a member.
Sorry for this lengthy process.
Stay safe one day at a time.  

And please write/email Serenityinpines@gmail.com
name: Warner Springs AA Discussion

description:
We welcome beginners, long-timers, and everyone in-between. The meeting features group participation on selected passages from the book Living Sober.

Closed meeting. Attendance at closed meetings is limited to persons who have a desire to stop drinking. If you think you have a problem with alcohol, you are welcome to attend this meeting.

We abide by the 12 Traditions and ask attendees to not take screenshots or recording of any kind. We do not sign court slips or offer proof of attendance.

description:
In Depth Big Book Study Group / Meeting

Our Group follows the Traditions and define our objectives with the Preamble

AA PREAMBLE
Alcoholics Anonymous is a fellowship of people who share their experience, strength and hope with each other, that they may solve their common problem and help others to recover from alcoholism. The only requirement for membership is a desire to stop drinking. There are no dues or fees for AA membership; we are self-supporting through our own contributions. AA is not allied with any sect, denomination, politics, organization or institution; does not wish to engage in any controversy; neither endorses nor opposes any causes. Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety.
name: Saturday Back to Basics Big Book Study

description:
1st Things 1st - Serious subject, Joyful Day!

We meet EVERY day, 365 days/year at 7:00am U.S. Central Time (5am Pacific / 8am Eastern).  

This is a closed meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous, meaning that it is for those who have a desire to stop drinking.

On Tuesdays, we have a topic, 
on Wednesday, we choose a step, and 
on Sundays, we have speakers. 

We are certainly not a glum lot! We average about 100 attendees every day and have a great group of people, predominantly from the US but across the globe as well. 
We begin our meeting with the long version of the serenity prayer, January 6th thought for the day, How it Works, the AA Preamble, offer big books to those who cannot afford them, and have a healthy mix of sobriety from 24 hours to 40 years. Most importantly, we like to have fun, because we are all alive!
name: 1st Things 1st

description:
Daily Zoom meetings at 12pm Thailand Time. (evenings for USA time zones, mornings for UK and Europe)

The Thailand Sobriety Group Online is an English speaking AA group that welcomes people from anywhere who want recovery from alcoholism. We especially focus on helping new members discover the program of AA through use of AA approved literature. We have a "meeting after the meeting" following every regular meeting for fellowship, question and answer and casual recovery chat.

- English speaking meeting
- Global meeting
- Meeting attendance verification available

TSGO MEETING THEMES BY DAY:
Monday: Speaker Meeting with discussion.
Tuesday: Big Book Reading in order with discussion.
Wednesday: 12 & 12 Step Essay Reading of chairpersons choice with discussion.
Thursday: Big Book or AA approved literature reading topic with discussion.
Friday: 12 & 12 Step Essay Readings in order with discussion.
Saturday: Big Book Reading with discussion. Chairpersons choice.
Sunday: First Step meeting. Readings from AA approved literature with discussion
name: 12pm AA - Thailand Sobriety Group Online

description:
Bienvenida/o a Alcohólicos Anónimos R.I.S Chile RIS en línea/ONLINE (Reuniones de Internacionales y Solitarios) es un servicio que proporcionan miembros de la comunidad de AA de Chile, para mantenerse sobrios y ayudar a aquellos(as) que buscan ayuda a su problema con el alcohol, pero que por algún motivo no pueden acudir a las reuniones presenciales como una de sus herramientas para alcanzar o mantener su sobriedad.
El contacto frecuente con otros alcohólicos, nuevos y veteranos, es una herramienta vital para nuestra recuperación. Sin embargo, algunos de nosotros(as) no siempre tenemos libre acceso a reuniones, ya sea por horario de trabajo, condiciones de salud, dificultades en la movilidad, condición de discapacidad sensorial, etc.. Nuestras experiencias a nivel mundial han demostrado que las reuniones en línea, son una buena alternativa. 

Números internacionales disponibles:  https://zoom.us/zoomconference
name: AA RIS Chile

description:
Sunshine at 7AM

We are a group based in South Florida, meeting daily @7am EST; sharing our experience, strength and hope. 
We read from the “Daily Reflections.” 
Saturday is a beginner’s meeting and Sunday is our speaker meeting. 
We celebrate anniversaries on the last Sunday of the month. 
We welcome all with open arms.

We meet Monday - Sunday at 7am Eastern Standard Time

Thursday: Twelve steps and twelve traditions Book Study
Friday:  Women’s Daily Reflection and sharing

description:
PREÁMBULO DE A.A.©
Alcohólicos Anónimos es una comunidad de hombres y mujeres que comparten su mutua experiencia, fortaleza y esperanza para resolver su problema común y ayudar a otros a recuperarse del alcoholismo.
El único requisito para ser miembro de A.A. es el deseo de dejar la bebida. Para ser miembro de A.A. no se pagan honorarios ni cuotas; nos mantenemos con nuestras propias contribuciones.
A.A. no está afiliada a ninguna secta, religión, partido político, organización o institución alguna; no desea intervenir en controversias; no respalda ni se opone a ninguna causa. Nuestro objetivo primordial es mantenernos sobrios y ayudar a otros alcoholicós a alcanzar el estado de sobriedad.

Reprinted with permission

description:

Liars Club reminder: "The events in our lives are important, but how we practice the principles of AA on these events is why this meeting is here. As a group, we ask that you speak about your experience, strength, and hope with AA's Steps & Traditions. Please keep your sharing to 3 minutes or less. It is my job to ask you to end if you go longer than 3 minutes.

description:
Conscious Contact Online meets on Sundays at 8PM EST. The first 40 minutes are open discussion and the last 20 minutes are spent in guided meditation. No special knowledge of meditation is needed and we are theologically agnostic. We deeply embrace the concepts of a loving Higher Power, a respect for each persons journey and believe that the Steps are not something we do so much as something that we become. Our meetings are informal and all are welcome to attend!

We are the online Sister group of the in-person Conscious Contact group which meets in York, PA on Wednesdays at 8PM.
name: Conscious Contact Online

description:

We also provide opportunities for people to get sponsors. Everyone is welcome to attend, and "the only requirement for AA membership is the desire to stop drinking".
This meeting is secure and a safe place.
Business meetings are held on the first Tuesday of every month.

If the waiting room is enabled please be patient and we will let you in shortly.

We are based in Peterborough, Ontario, Canada and we welcome all to our little city!

name: The Lunch Club

description:
Our A.A. group is physically based in the beautiful volcanic and scenic town of Tagaytay, Cavite. 

We meet Wednesday, Friday, & Sunday.  

Wednesday's meeting is on open discussion focused on the reading of the Big Book. We read two pages of the Big Book every Wednesday, starting at the beginning of the book, page by page, until the end of the book (excluding the stories). The topic is then based on the reading.  

The fourth Wednesday, Friday, or Sunday will be a speaker meeting followed by open discussion.  

All other meetings will be open discussion on a topic of the leader's choice. 

Please log in to a registered Zoom account to successfully connect to our meeting.
name: AA Cavite

description:
This group of A.A. attempts to maintain a tradition of free expression, and conduct a meeting where alcoholics may feel free to express any doubts or disbeliefs they may have, and to share their own personal form of spiritual experience, their search for it, or their rejection of it. We do not endorse or oppose any form of religion or atheism. Rather we strive to cultivate an atmosphere of respect for believers and nonbelievers alike, with an eye toward mindfulness and unity so that we may focus on a shared solution to alcoholism. Our only wish is to assure suffering alcoholics that they can find sobriety in A.A. without having to accept anyone else's beliefs or having to deny their own.

Public Email Contact: aa.wild1s@gmail.com
name: Wild Ones

description: We provide a safe place for newcomers and long timers to share their experience, strength and hope.:
name: Hawaii Online Meetings

description: This weekly meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous attempts to maintain a tradition of free expression and conduct a meeting where alcoholics may feel free to express themselves about their own experiences, beliefs, or feelings (including any doubts or disbeliefs they may have). As freethinkers, we aspire to open-mindedness and to appreciating the sharing of others.  As a group, we are secular.  That is, we do not endorse or oppose any system of belief, nor do we have any quarrel with any form of religion.  Our only wish is to assure suffering alcoholics that they can find sobriety in A.A. without having to accept anyone else's belief or having to deny their own.
name: Freethinkers Living Sober

Nuestro único propósito es asegurar a los alcohólicos/as que puedan encontrar la sobriedad en A.A. sin tener que aceptar las creencias de nadie más o tener que negar las propias.
name: Ateos y agnósticos en españols

description:
Aloha,
"Ohana" is a Hawaiian word that means something like "extended family". Our group is based in Hawaii and in keeping with the spirit of "aloha" we welcome attendees and members from all over the world. We meet every day, twice a day, at 8am and 8pm Hawaii time. The format varies and includes speaker/discussion and book studies. Only alcoholics may participate but respectful visitors are also welcome to attend.

description:
Women candlelight meeting 5 nights a week at 8 pm EST.

Sunday is leader discussion meeting,

Monday is Step 11 Meditation,

Tuesday is Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions book,

Wednesday is “Plain Language Big Book: A Tool for Reading Alcoholics Anonymous” (the new AA General Service Conference-approved literature published in 2024) , and

Thursday is leader discussion meeting.

We encourage use of video in our meeting so we can all stay better connected and use the Waiting Room to provide a safe meeting for all participants. 

We rotate our 10 service positions every 3 months, so lots of service opportunities are available. We will "sign slips" by sending an email back to you provided you attend the full meeting; just ask the chair.
name: AA Women's Carry This Message Candlelight Meeting

description:
Welcome, Friends! We are really glad you found us! We are an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous that welcomes newcomers & those returning from a relapse, long-timers, and everyone in between.

We meet every evening at 9p central time. 
Sundays we host a speaker, 
Mondays we study the 12 x 12, 
Fridays we study the Big Book & 
Saturdays are for the Symphonies! 
The other nights are open discussion on various topics & themes. 

Feel free to join us 30 minutes before the meeting and/or stay late for Fellowship! 

We take sobriety seriously, but at the same time, we are a rowdy bunch that likes to have fun, so come trudge the road of happy destiny with us!

No password, waiting room enabled. Closed Captioning (CC) available.

For those needing meeting verification: We will announce how to receive them during the meeting introduction.
name: AA Awesome

description:
The Twilight Zone is a meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous that meets seven nights a week.  The formal meeting is open for one hour and then we go into the "After Party" for those who wish to stay for continued fellowship.  We stay open until anyone who wishes to share gets an opportunity to do so.  

Saturday and Sundays are speaker meetings where an invited member shares their experience, strength and hope and chooses a topic for the group to share.  We stay open for the weekend "After Party".

Our Twilight Zone is unique in that we follow a tag format.  When it's time to share, each member randomly chooses another.  If chosen, each member can share if they wish to or pass it to another. We let the spirit of the group guide us! 

Zoom Meeting Time: 10:30pm EST - Every Night

description:
We welcome you to join us in a safe and loving environment where we focus on recovery from alcoholism. You will meet people counting days as well as those with years of sobriety. Newcomers are welcome and encouraged to share and get active in AA.  Please join our closed meeting, open to anyone who has a desire to stop drinking.  We meet seven (7) days a week at 5 PM Eastern Time.
We do send email meeting verification for attending.
Monday: Lead share on As Bill Sees It
Tuesday: Lead share on a Daily Reflections
Wednesday: We discuss the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions
Thursday: We discuss the Third Step
Friday: Lead share on Topic
Saturday: We discuss the Big Book 
Sunday: We have a speaker meeting. The speaker has 40 minutes.

We hold an anniversary meeting on the last weekday of every month. Shares on how you’re staying sober.
We hold a group conscience meeting on the first Monday of every month  following our regular meeting starting at 6:10 PM (Eastern Time).
name: AA Love & Tolerance NYC

description:
The AA Thailand International Meeting is a weekly English speaking Closed AA Speaker Discussion meeting based in Pattaya, Thailand. We are a true International meeting, with local European & American Expats & visitors welcome. 

At the start of each meeting we read How it Works, then Daily Reflections. A speaker then shares their ESH for about 20 minutes then it goes to the floor for sharing. We observe AA's primary purpose, have no affiliation outside of AA, and we do our best to observe our AA Traditions.
name: AA Thailand International Meeting
Freedom from Bondage Big Book Study

description:
We are a zoom group from the small town of Waitsburg Washington, USA.  Most of our members have over 20 years of sobriety (some over 40), but we are always looking for new folks to which we can pass on some of our wisdom, and who can help us remember "what it was like".  
Join us every night at 8pm Pacific.

description:
The New Rush Hour Relief Group started on October 18, 1991. Located in the heart of Atlanta just off the 75/85 interstates at All Saints Episcopal Church. While adapting to global pandemic, the meetings are being held on Zoom.

The group meets four days a week (Mon - Thurs)
M - Speaker/ Open Discussion
T- Steps and Traditions Study
W - Open Discussion
Thurs - Big Book Study
All Are Welcome.

description:
Daily Zoom/Telephone meeting. We start the meeting by taking turns reading conference approved literature, then sharing on the topic. Open to all; everyone is welcome to attend. Meets 7:30am ET daily, 7 days a week, for 1 hour. Usually open ~15 minutes before/after for fellowship.

Attendance verification via email is available.

Medical and psychology professionals and students are welcome to attend. 
Please email us in advance so we can send you some information.

description:
Turning Point is an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
We are based in Boston and include members from around the country and the world.
All are welcome.
We meet Monday through Friday mornings from 7 to 8 a.m. ET. 

Monday we read from Living Sober. 
Tuesday is a Speaker/Discussion format. 
Wednesday we read from the 12 & 12. 
Thursday we practice gratitude. 
Friday we read the stories at the back of the Big Book.

description:
Morning Meditation/Evening Reflections (MM/ER) is an on-line home group of Alcoholics Anonymous and we meet every day, 7 days a week, at 6:45am EST to share our experience, strength and hope with each other, and we are especially glad to welcome newcomers.

At the Morning Meditation meeting, every participant has the opportunity to introduce themselves to the group before the morning reading from the 24 Hours a Day book followed by one minute shares from as many participants as possible after the reading. Sponsors are always available at our meetings.  Meeting Verifications on request.

Doors open at 6am EST for fellowship.  Meeting starts promptly at 6:45am EST

description:
Dawn Patrol is an open Alcoholics Anonymous meeting and all are welcome to attend, especially newcomers. 
Open meetings are available to anyone interested in Alcoholics Anonymous’ program of recovery from alcoholism. Nonalcoholics may attend open meetings as observers.

Dawn Patrol meets every day of the year with topics including AA literature

-Tuesday is a Step or Tradition study

-Thursday is a speaker meeting; anyone with a year of sobriety may sign up to speak.

-Saturday is a Big Book study

If you do not have a home group we invite you to become a member of Dawn Patrol [by attending] our Group Conscience [which] meets the second Saturday of the month at 7:45 AM [Mountain Time].
name: Dawn Patrol

We are an online A.A. home group and welcome all who suffer from alcoholism.
We have an A.A. speaker for the first 30 minutes then we open up for round robin discussion.  If you think you might have a problem with alcohol, you are welcome here.  There is a solution.  
Come hear the A.A. message of hope and stay so that you may pass it on.


Public Email Contact: howitworks21228@gmail.com
name: How it Works 21228

description:
Aloha On Awakening is an AA group hosting a daily morning meeting from Honolulu, Hawaii. We are a literature-based group using “Daily Reflections” as the basis for our discussion. Our format is to read the day’s reading from the book “Daily Reflections” and then open the meeting for discussion on the day’s reading. Our daily meetings are open meetings and all are welcome to attend. No password is required when using the OIAA shortcut. We meet 7 days a week at 6:30 AM-7:30 AM (HST/UTC-10).

ON AWAKENING, MEETING INFO
Like this meeting and want to return? We meet seven days a week 6:30–7:30 a.m. HST
name: Aloha On Awakening

description:
El "Grupo Matinal 365 " es un grupo on line de Alcohólicos Anónimos en español. El grupo es libre, gratuito y virtual a través de Zoom. Sesionamos los 365 días del año de 10 a 12h, GMT +2. 
El grupo es muy útil para aquellos que, por cualquier motivo, no puedan asistir a reuniones presenciales. 
El tipo de reunión es temática, y cada día compartimos experiencia, sobre un texto de nuestra literatura. 
Los libros que empleamos para discusión y estudio son : el texto básico, viviendo sobrio, doce pasos y doce tradiciones, manual de Servicios sección España, como lo ve bill, folletos informativos, y Alcohólicos Anónimos llega a su mayoría de edad. 

grupomatinal365@gmail.com

Reuniones  tematicas de A.A. donde participan los Alcoholicos y puede asistir cualquier persona que este interesada en Alcohólicos Anónimos o desee saber si tiene problemas con la bebida
name: Grupo Matinal 365

description:
The Lopsided Triangle is a collection of AA members from around the Pacific Region. 
From the beginning, our primary purpose has been to open conversations around important topics and create interesting and relevant information to the fellowship. 
In response to the COVID-19 Pandemic, the group has evolved from a concepts study group into a steering committee dedicated to providing helpful resources and content to the fellowship at large. 
The meeting is a panel format with 3 speakers, Q&A, with time for open sharing with a focus on Barriers to Recovery.  Our goal remains to help our respective locales and continue to open the fellowship to more eyes, ears, bodies, hearts and minds.

description:
All are welcome to the Beginner's Book Study Meeting. Our readings are displayed on the screen for all to read, and closed captioning is available. We meet here daily because we have found that connections are protections. Love & tolerance is our code, so we are all-inclusive. Our goal is to stay sober and help others to achieve sobriety. If you are having problems related to alcohol, we can help. Our meetings are as scheduled below.

1. On Mondays & Fridays we read from and discuss a reading from the first 164 pages of the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous 4th edition.  
2. On Tuesdays we read and discuss a reading from the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions. The last Tuesday of the month is a Tradition reading correlating with that month.    
3. On Wednesdays we have a beginner's topic discussion in which we will read and discuss for the remainder of the hour. (Any Conference Approved Literature from our web page)  
4. On Thursdays we read and discuss an article from the Grapevine Magazine.
5. On Saturdays we read and discuss a reading from the personal stories of those that came before us from pages 170 to 559 of the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous.  
6. On (Sundays) we read the stories from those that came before us in the book "Experience, Strength, And Hope," by Bill W.
name: Beginners Book Study Meeting

description:
Learn to Meditate Today!  We lovingly call the meeting "Meditation 101" because of how simple meditation can be. Come get a Checkup from the Neck Up!

We have 3 Meditation Meetings:
Thurs - 8:15 am ET
Sat - 11:30 am ET
Sun - 7 am ET

Don't think you have time in your day to meditate? Are you having problems meditating or relaxing? Did you know that you can start meditating very early in your sobriety? Do you think meditation is too complicated for you? If so, you should join us and see just how simple meditation really is. You can meditate in your car or laying in bed. You can meditate at any time and any place!

“Perhaps one of the greatest rewards of meditation and prayer is the sense of belonging that comes to us. We no longer live in a completely hostile world. We are no longer lost and frightened and purposeless.” (12 & 12 pg. 105)

Join us as we go thru the 12 Steps in 4 hours on Zoom. 1-hour Workshop monthly also. 

Come get Virtual Chips and tell us how many days/months/years you have! Get a 1-Minute Chip! How about a Zoo Crew Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip? Everyone's time is important!

Join our Service Team. We'll train you. E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com.
name: A Simple Way to Meditate & Get Your Mind Right

description:
Real Talk Recovery meets on Zoom daily to fulfill the primary purpose of AA, to stay connected with the fellowship, and to support the daily maintenance of our spiritual condition.

Our meeting starts at 7:05 PM EST and runs until 8:15.  The meeting room opens at 6:45 PM EST and stays open until 8:30 for fellowshipping in the "virtual parking lot" before and after the meeting.

Each night has a different chairperson and different format:

Sun - Big Book Study
Mon - Meditation & Open Discussion
Tue - Newcomer/ Beginners Meeting
Wed - Daily Reflections
Thu - 12 Step/12 Traditions Study
Fri - Music Inspiration/ Final Friday Anniversaries
Sat - Emotional Sobriety

description:
Welcome to the First 24, an open meeting of AA. We are focused on the newcomer or anyone coming back from a slip. The meeting is originated from the Eastern Townships of Quebec at the tip of the Appalachian mountain range. Although we are virtual, this area is where we find our spirituality and be closer to our High Power. 

We would love to share our experiences, strengths and hopes with each other in an open discussion. Everyone is welcome.

Saturday Mornings from 9am to 10am EST
name: The First 24

description:
Meetings available every day 7 days a week! 

Monday – As Bill Sees It
Tuesday – Daily Reflections 
Wednesday – Open Topic 
Thursday – Big Book
Friday – 12 & 12 (except for the fourth Friday of the month which we’ll read the Tradition of the month from the 12 and 12) 
Saturday – Open Topic (except for the fourth Saturday of the month which will be a speaker meeting) 
Sunday – Living Sober/Came to Believe Morning meetings are literature meetings and afternoon is open topic every day!

description:
Welcome all alcoholics—newcomers, old-timers and those in-between. Our literature-based discussion meeting focuses on AA's singleness of purpose: recovery from alcoholism. We look forward to seeing you and sharing with you!

No password is needed to join this meeting. You will enter a waiting room, and the chairperson will admit you.

Monday - Daily Reflections
Tuesday - Literature Based Topic (Open Discussion)
Wednesday - Chairperson’s Choice
Thursday - Big Book Study (We'll read a few paragraphs out of the Big Book and open the floor for discussion

description:
*AA GUTS* (AA Grant Us the Serenity) is an online Zoom meeting that welcomes anyone who has a desire to stop drinking.
The GUTS marathon meeting is held every night at 7:00PM PST - 2:00AM EST. 
At the top of each hour, the meeting resets and rotates Hosts.
This meeting is held 7 nights per week and 7 meetings per night.

Court verification available This is a safe and anonymous environment that follows the traditions of Alcoholics Anonymous to help the alcoholic who still suffers. All are welcome.

AA Literature - https://aaguts.com/#literature
You will not be able to enter the room without a Zoom account. Please make any necessary changes to include a verified email within your Zoom settings. These are the instructions for creating a Zoom account.

A valid Zoom account is required to access this meeting.

description:
Join us twice a week as we focus on Steps 6 & 7.  Come see how Step 10 is interlinked with Steps 6 & 7.  Come get your check-up from the neck up and get your mind right!

We Host 7 meetings 7 days a week in the same room.  Spend the day with the Original Zoo Crew!
The Original Zoo Crew started on Zoom in March of 2020. When the world shut down, we opened our Virtual Doors!

We are going on a Sober Cruise in May of 2023. Join us!

Sun at 9 pm EST - We listen to a 4 minute video by Sandy Beach where he mentions "dropping the rock."  We then have an Open Discussion.

Tues at 5 pm EST - We read the Drop the Rock book line by line and then have an Open Discussion.

Let's "drop the rock" that's weighing us down: fear, anger, resentment, dishonesty, etc... Is there something you want freedom from? Alcohol was never the problem; Steps 6 & 7 work on the real problem, me and my character defects!

(BB pg. 64) "Our liquor was but a symptom. So we had to get down to causes and conditions." Steps 6 & 7 are the crux of the AA way of life.

Passcode: zoo

Join us each month as we go thru the 12 Steps in 4 hours on Zoom. We also have a 1-houjr Recovery Workshop every month.

Come get Virtual Chips and tell us how many days/months/years you have! How about a Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip? Everyone's time is important!

Join our Service Team. E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com.
name: Drop the Rock Letting Go of Character Defects

Let's "drop the rock" that's weighing us down: fear, anger, resentment, dishonesty, etc... Is there something you want freedom from? Alcohol was never the problem; Steps 6 & 7 work on the real problem, me and my character defects!

(BB pg. 64) "Our liquor was but a symptom. So we had to get down to causes and conditions." Steps 6 & 7 are the crux of the AA way of life.

Passcode: zoo

Join us each month as we go thru the 12 Steps in 4 hours on Zoom. We also have a 1-houjr Recovery Workshop every month.

Come get Virtual Chips and tell us how many days/months/years you have! How about a Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip? Everyone's time is important!

Join our Service Team. E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com.
name: Drop the Rock Letting Go of Character Defects

description:
We are a virtual group which was set up as an open meeting for newcomers and others to explore the ideas and principles of AA through the "Big Book" and other AA literature.  Readings are posted so you don't need the books to join.  All are welcome - newcomer to old timer.

You will find this a fun, informal meeting, limited to 40 participants, where you will have a chance to share and ask questions, or just listen - your choice.  

We start each meeting with a 5-minute meditation, followed by the daily readings and then sharing.  The door is locked at the beginning of the meeting, or when we are full, so come early.

description:
We Are Knowlton Serenity - Find, Strengthen, and Enjoy Sobriety with Us
An Open Meeting of Alcoholic Anonymous
There is always hope and another way to go about your life. You are not alone. Addiction to alcohol can have a crippling effect on you and those around you and can lead to health problems and behavioral disorders. But there’s always hope and there is always light, even in the darkest of hours.

Our weekly meeting is scheduled for every Sunday Morning. At this meeting we focus on a story of experience, strength and hope. The floor is then opened to acknowledge our speaker.

Open Speaker Meeting Every Sunday 10AM to 11:15AM EST
Closed Women's Meeting Every Monday 4PM to 5PM EST
name: Knowlton Serenity

description:
Secular Serenity is currently the only secular AA meeting in Cape Town South Africa. This is an open meeting and all are welcome. 
The meeting was established in November 2017 to widen the AA gateway so that all who suffer may pass through and find long-term sobriety in A.A. 
regardless of their belief or lack of belief in a higher power.
name: Secular Serenity

description:
Hello from beautiful sunny Saint Augustine Florida. Our group was started in the world  famous Cathedral Basilica church on the Plaza de la Constitución 35 years ago. One of the coolest things about our group has been almost every meeting we had out of town visitors. We know how to welcome guests, look forward to having you join us for a meeting today!
All of our meetings start at noon and are open. If you ‘think’ you have a problem or just want to know what happens in an AA meeting this is the place for you. We love to share our experience, strength and hope. 
Ok here’s the schedule:
**Monday is a general open discussion meeting, bring a topic or concern you have  and we’ll talk about it, great way to start the work week.
**Wednesday is our Big Book meeting. Currently we are reading the first 164 pages. We read about 15-20 minutes then do open discussion. 
**Saturday is our big meeting of the week, we have excellent speakers lined up each week, you don’t want to miss this one. It’s a speaker discussion, so the speaker shares his experience strength and hope for 20-25 minutes then we open it up for discussion. The meeting stays open for 30-45 minutes after so people can hang out for awhile.
name: A Night Owl Group in Saint Augustine Fl

description:
An online Book Study using the AA Big Book and 12 Steps and 12 Traditions. 
We read together and discuss how the reading applies to our experience, strength and hope - What we were like, what happened, and what we are like now. 
We welcome anyone to attend. 
Meets every Monday from 7PM to 8PM Pacific Time.
name: AA Book Journey

description: Newcomer meeting of AA which meets weekly at 6:00pm Eastern on Wednesday's to share experience, strength and hope with Newcomers in recovery. Meeting format is speaker discussion, with a 10 minute opening speaker and then general discussion about recovery from Alcoholism with a focus on the first three steps. This meeting is primarily so that newcomers with less than 90 days of sobriety have a place to meet and share the joys and challenges of early recovery. Beginners are encouraged to get a sponsor as soon as possible from other attendees that have a working knowledge of the twelve steps of recovery.
name: AA Newcomer Online Meeting

description:
Monday = Step 1 "We admitted that we are powerless over alcohol - that our lives had become unmanageable."  
Tuesday = Step 2 – "Came to believe that a power greater than ourselves could restore us to sanity."
Wednesday = Step 3 – "Made a decision to turn our will and our lives over to the care of God as we understood Him."  
Thursday = 9th Step Promises
Friday = Step 11 – "Sought through prayer and meditation to improve our conscious contact with God as we understood Him, praying only for knowledge of His will for us and the power to carry that out."  
Saturday = Recovery, Unity, and Service – "I am responsible - When anyone, anywhere, reaches out for help, I want the hand of A.A. always to be there. And for that: I am responsible."   
Sunday = Speaker’s Choice

Sunday = Speaker’s Choice

description:

Sometimes a page, a paragraph, and sentence, or even just a few words start a lively explanation. 
Bring a Big Book and a pen   -- you'll want to take notes. 
This is essentially a sparkling speaker meeting; occasionally there is time for questions at the end. 
Before CoVid, the meeting took place at Club Sebastian on US Hwy 1, and will return so when the clubhouse resumes full activity.
name: AA Big Book Detailed Study

description:

This is an historical in-person meeting which moved online during the pandemic.

description:
These Informal Gatherings" is an AA group focused on the solution for an Alcoholic found in the Dr's Opinion thru the first 164 pages of the book Alcoholics Anonymous. Our aim is to provide a safe place where Alcoholics can find the solution and fellowship they seek. We provide a 12 Step discussion, Traditions meeting, and a Speaker/ Participation meeting.
 We believe the 12 Traditions are to the group what the 12 Steps are to the Alcoholic, hence we intend to apply what the Traditions suggest.
 We are fully self supporting, and we are not affiliated with any outside organization.

Please "join us as we trudge the road of happy destiny!"

1 hr. long Open Meeting.
1st week of the Month is a Step Study,
2nd week of the Month is a Traditions Meeting,
Remaining weeks of the Month are Open topic discussion.
name: These Informal Gatherings

description:
As a SECULAR group, our meeting format does not include the recitation of any prayers or readings that invoke the name of any deity.  
The intent of this meeting is to provide a comfortable forum for those recovering from alcoholism who have difficulty in accepting the traditional or fundamental beliefs of God or Higher Power as outlined in the AA literature.  
All AA members are welcome.  Those having faith in a Higher Power and those having none are welcome to attend and participate in discussions.
name: Many Paths to Sobriety

description:

The purpose of this particular morning Attitude Adjustment meeting is to give A.A. members the opportunity to start their day with a rededication to sobriety and a spiritual way of life. 
This is not a meeting devoted to relieving the past, as to developing the appropriate attitudes for living this particular day successfully. 
We have a ten minute speaker then the floor is open for participation. 
No password required, waiting room enabled.

description:
Sunrise Zoom meets Monday through Friday.  It is the perfect way to start your day.  
On Monday, Wednesday and Friday we read from the 24 Hour a Day book followed by discussion.  
On Tuesday and Thursday we read from Daily Reflections followed by discussion.  
Our members are newly sober as well as members with years of sobriety. Our group is an even mix of men and women from various locales. 
Waiting room enabled.

description:
We are a daily Home Group based on the BB and the 12 & 12. 
We try to take the mystery out of the steps by doing a different step everyday. 

The meeting starts with a reading of selected paragraphs from the BB followed by sharing. 
The second half starts with announcements and a reading from the 12&12. 

The meeting opens 30 minutes early and stays open 30 minutes after for fellowship. 
Court Verification, chips and books are available. Password is required.
name: Happy Joyous and Free

description:
Open AA meeting established March 2020 with daily meetings originating from New Orleans at 7:15 am CST. 
Attendance verification is provided upon request.

Daily Meetings include:
Tuesday, Wednesday and Sunday are AA Literature meetings.
Monday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday are speaker discussion meetings or moderator's choice, usually emphasizing the principles of the program or other AA tools.

All are Invited to attend, listeners are welcomed, and sharing is voluntary. 
We welcome all who wish to join us as we carry the message of recovery to fellow alcoholics.
name: Eye Openers Online

description: We read small sections of the book 12 Steps and 12 Traditions. We go through one tradition a week. We then open the meeting to group discussion on the weekly topic. Free online copies of the 12x12 can be found here:  https://www.aa.org/pages/en_US/twelve-steps-and-twelve-traditions   Closed meeting. We abide by the 12 Traditions and ask attendees to not take screenshots or recording of any kind. We do not sign court slips or offer proof of attendance.
name: One Tradition At A Time (1DAAT)

description: جلسه الکلی های گمنام فارسی زبان همدلان هر روز ساعت ۳:۳۰ بعد ازظهر به وقت گرینویچ‌ (بوقت انگلستان) بمدت ۹۰ دقیقه برگزار می‌شود. گروه به همه افراد از سرتاسر جهان(با هر گرایش مذهبی، جنسیتی، نژادی و اجتماعی) تنها با داشتن تمایل به قطع مصرف الکل خوش آمد می‌گوید. در جلسه روزانه چند سطر از کتاب بزرگ خوانده می‌شود وسخنران بمدت ۲۰دقیقه در مورد تجربه خود صحبت می کند و سپس جلسه برای مشارکت اعضایی که تمایل دارند باز می‌شود. موضوعات جلسات بصورت متنوع و روزانه می‌باشد. ضمنا روزهای یکشنبه تولد هوشیاری سالیانه اعضا برگزار میشود.

description:
Esta reunión virtual solo se lleva a cabo los dias domingos y dura una hora aproximadamente, el tema principal es taller de pactica de paso 11 oracion y meditación.

1. Se hace el preambulo y se lleva la guia con las lecturas (15 - 20 min)

2. Se hace meditacion. (20 min)

3. Se comparte entre los compañeros las expericias que les trae este paso durante la meditacion o en el trascurso de su recuperación. (20 min aproximadamente)
name: Grupo Virtual Servir es Vivir

description: A weekly Traditions Study Zoom meeting focusing on learning more about, and discussing, the Traditions of Alcoholics Anonymous.  Open to all; everyone is welcome to attend. Please join us as we get into the 12 Traditions of this amazing fellowship!  Our base meeting is AA GUTS (Grant Us The Serenity), but all are welcome to attend.
name: AA GUTS Traditions Study Meeting

description:
This one-hour meeting is very newcomer friendly, especially those needing attendance verification. Voluntary sharing only at this meeting, no one will be called upon to share.

Cameras are not required but must be on to be unmuted. If you would like your camera on at any time during the meeting, please turn it on during the pre-meeting before the speaker begins. No new videos will be allowed on once the meeting begins.

Everyone is welcome to attend. Attendance verification given on request . Every meeting is a speaker meeting with recommended speakers
from all over the world.

We meet every Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday at 2:30 pm pacific, 5:30 pm eastern, 10:30 pm UK.

description:
We are an international group of grateful alcoholics, who love the AA way of life. Our meeting is based in Dublin, Ireland and our hope is to help the newcomer and to inspire other alcoholics, as we trudge the Road to Happy Destiny. 

The format of this meeting is closed/discussion. At times we have a speaker, who leads our discussion for 10-15 minutes.  Other times we read a bit from the literature to inspire sharing and then we open the meeting for discussion.

Newcomers, YOU are ALWAYS welcome! In fact, YOU ARE the MOST IMPORTANT PERSON IN THE ROOM! You are the lifeblood of AA as without you there would be no us! We do ask that newcomers have your cameras on. We kindly ask this of you, so we can properly welcome you to this wonderful fellowship & to put a face with a name!

We do offer court verification for those of us who need it. The host will explain how that happens. Are you looking for a service
commitment? Look no further! We are always in need of trusted servants and we provide training for any service involving the use of Zoom. 

From all of us at HATW, WELCOME HOME! We look forward to seeing you real soon soon!
name: Hands Across the Water

description:
"This group of A.A. attempts to maintain a tradition of free expression and conduct a meeting where alcoholics may feel free to express any doubts or dis-beliefs they may have, and to share their own personal experience.  We do not endorse or oppose any form of religion or atheism. Our only wish is to assure suffering alcoholics that they can find sobriety in A.A. without having to accept anyone else beliefs or having to deny their own."
A.A. Group #431993 Area 73 District 04

description:
We have organized a meeting through Group Conscience.  
The meeting begins with introductions, the Preamble, announcements and 10 minutes of guided meditation, then our Chair has selected a speaker who will share their story or a reading related to their 11 step experience for about 10-15 minutes.  
After about a 25 minute open discussion period, we end the meeting with another 10 minute guided meditation and then close with the serenity prayer.
name: Bill's 11th Step Meditation

description:
Speakers Through Speakers is a weekly meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. Each week we digitally convert and listen to an old AA speaker tape that was sent to us, making sure the sound quality is okay and noting any anonymity breaks to edit out, we then upload the talk to the internet, thus saving it for future generations of AAs. Our mission is to save these old talks, that carry the message so well, that might otherwise have been lost.

• There is a brief participation portion at each meeting, please take notes of your favorite parts / ideas / principles etc. during a talk to share about later.

* Please turn on your camera when entering the meeting to help us know you're not a bomber.

• If you or someone you know has a bunch of old AA speaker cassettes that might not be online yet, or you're interested in helping convert tapes or starting another STS mtg on another night, please email speakersthroughspeakers@gmail.com
name: Speakers Through Speakers - Speaker Tape & Discussion

description:
On Awakening (OA) is an open Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) meeting. We are an opening and friendly bunch that welcomes beginners, long-timers, and everyone in-between especially newcomers!!! OA meets every day using the tools of the AA program to get and stay sober. We have a different format each day with our group conscience meeting the first Friday of the month after the meeting. 

Sunday: As Bill Sees It
Monday: Daily Reflections 
Tuesday: Open Discussion 
Wednesday: Big Book 
Thursday: Living Sober 
Friday: Steps & Traditions 
Saturday: Step11/Meditation 

Once you have entered the meeting please press *6 to mute/share, *9 to raise your hand.

Don’t be shy and come on in!
name: On Awakening Group

description:
This is an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous for women who have a desire to stop drinking. 

If you think you have a problem with drinking, please join us for connection and support in achieving or growing sobriety. 
We discuss and share the solution as laid out in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
We grow healthier and happier in sobriety, in our everyday lives-together. 
We are friendly, sincere and welcoming. Look forward to seeing you soon! The Women of Back Porch Meetings
name: Back Porch Women's

description:
A daily online support  Zoom meeting with readings & open discussion from The Daily Reflection, AA Big Book, & more. We are not a glum lot. Grounded in the Steps & Traditions of AA, we share our Experience Strength & Hope with Newcomers & Old Timers alike.

Tradition #3 in Alcoholics Anonymous states, "The only requirement for membership is the desire to stop drinking." Open to all; everyone is welcome to attend. Meets daily from 10 pm to 12 am USA EST. If you want to get sober or if you’re feeling tempted, talk with us. If you just want to listen in, come on in.
name: AA After Hours

description:
The 50in50 Group of Alcoholics Anonymous (GSO number:000368180)

We are a group of Alcoholics Anonymous. Our members try to adhere to the Traditions of Alcoholic Anonymous to the best of our abilities. We are not allied with any sect, denomination, politics, organization or institution and we do not endorse nor oppose any outside causes. We keep to the primary purpose of Alcoholics Anonymous - to stay sober and to help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety.

As a group, we seek to go to 50 meetings in 50 states via videoconference. We hold a speaker/discussion meeting on Sundays at 9pm EST on Zoom.  All are welcome.
name: 50in50 Group

description:
This Is It Women's Group is a Beginner's Step Study: the 1st week we talk about the 1st step, the 2nd week the 2nd step, the 3rd week the 3rd step, the 4th week we do a wrap-up. If there happens to be a 5th week, we have a Speaker’s Choice topic. 

We are a Women's Group of Alcoholics Anonymous. Our primary purpose is to carry AA's message to the alcoholic who still suffers. We have no outside affiliation nor do we endorse, finance, or lend the A.A. name to any related facility or outside enterprise, lest problems of money, property, and prestige divert us from our primary purpose.

The meeting starts at 7 pm CST but we open at 6:30 pm CST for fellowship. We also stay open 30 minutes after the meeting for fellowship as well.
name: This Is It - Women's Beginner's Step Study

We are a registered group with Alcoholics Anonymous meeting every evening at 8:30pm EST / 7:30 pm CST / 5:30pm PST. Our Room opens 15min early for fellowship and introductions.  No passcode - waiting room enabled.
These are 90 minute meetings 8:30pm ET to 10:00pm EST

description:
Our group studies the Big Book of “Alcoholics Anonymous” and the “Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions.” 
We are an open A.A. meeting and everyone is welcome. 
The first part of our meeting is a book study, led by a live facilitator or a recording of a facilitator. The remaining time is open for sharing experience, strength and hope related to the Step or Tradition being studied that day. We are a mixture of new-comers and old-timers and everything in between, with a common love for our literature and the solution of the
12 Steps of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
Captions, Daily Service Opportunities and Attendance Verification are available.
name: The Way Out

description:
A daily online support  Zoom meeting with readings & open discussion from The Daily Reflection, AA Big Book, & more. We are not a glum lot. Grounded in the Steps & Traditions of AA, we share our Experience Strength & Hope with Newcomers & Old Timers alike.
Tradition #3 in Alcoholics Anonymous states, "The only requirement for membership is the desire to stop drinking." Open to all; everyone is welcome to attend. Meets daily from 10 pm to 12 am USA EST. If you want to get sober or if you’re feeling tempted, talk with us. If you just want to listen in, come on in.

ALL are welcome (you do NOT need to identify as queer to attend). 
We meet Tuesday nights from 6pm - 7pm (ET). Please email QueerMCs@gmail.com for passcode.

Week 1: Speaker
Week 2: Living Sober
Week 3: Step Speaker
Week 4: MC's Choice (Chair chooses reading from AA literature)
Week 5: Show and Tell (Member shares a piece of text, music, or other form of art - and speaks to how it relates to their recovery)

description:
We meet Thursdays at 9:00 p.m. - 10:00 p.m. Eastern time (except on the last Thursday of every month we end at 10:15 p.m. Eastern time).
 We are an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
Our format is to open with a speaker who shares their experience, strength and hope on a selected piece of A.A. literature followed by a Q and A, a brief secretaries break, then ending with an open discussion. 

We are grounded in the Twelve Steps, Twelve Traditions and Twelve Concepts of Alcoholics Anonymous, which allows for a wide variety of A.A. topics on any given Thursday night, but no matter what there is the primary purpose of the A.A. message and a chance to connect.
name: Mighty Purpose and Rhythm Group

description: Somos um grupo de Alcoólicos Anónimos Online, cujo o objectivo é levar a Mensagem e o Programa de Recuperação de AA aos alcoólicos que não têm ou não podem participar em reuniões presenciais nos seus locais de residência em Portugal Continental e Ilhas (Madeira e Açores), bem como àqueles que estão imigrados em outros países. Temos como missão também levar a Mensagem e o Programa de Recuperação de AA aos alcoólicos que residem nos países de expressão portuguesa em África (PALOP), Cabo Verde, São Tomé e Príncipe, Guiné-Bissau, Angola and Moçambique.

description:

We are based in the Houston area, Texas.
The first Saturday of the month is our birthday and Traditions Study.
The second Saturday of the month is a 30 minute speaker (followed by discussion) meeting.
All other meetings are discussion topic meetings.
We have a sobriety span of 1 day to 56 years of sobriety.
name: SATURDAY SISTERS WOMEN'S AA MEETING

description:
This group reads Steps 3, 7 and 11 in succession throughout the month. If a first-time newcomer joins the meeting, Group Conscience has decided the First Step will be read overriding the scheduled step that evening. The format for the final Thursday(s) of the month is chairperson's choice. Suggestions include selecting a reading from A.A conference-approved literature followed by group discussion; inviting a speaker to share their experience with the Third, Seventh, or Eleventh Step; or creating a topic related to the Third, Seventh or Eleventh Step and facilitating a discussion. No passcode necessary. Waiting Room enabled.
Closed "Thanksgiving Day (US) and Christmas Day"
name: A Spiritual Journey – Steps 3-7-11

Venmo link for donations and literature links will be provided,
We do validate for courts if the attendee participates with a camera on.

description:
We are a Pre-Covid group of Alcoholics Anonymous with members from all over the world. All our meetings are in English, and are open meetings. We welcome all visitors and newcomers. We take great care to cater for newcomers and at the end of our meetings we have optional breakout rooms for those who may be shy to speak in front of the whole group. We also provide meeting attendance verification.

Occasionally we experience Zoom Bombers, so we have a protocol to protect members from this experience. Our meetings are “hand raising only” for those who wish to share, and if you want to introduce yourself or speak, you will be asked to turn on your camera initially. However, you do not have to turn on your camera at any stage if you want to just listen.

The default setting on Zoom is “Speaker view” and this is recommended over “Gallery View” during the meeting, as this also deters bomber disruption. These simple measures enable us to provide a safe space for alcoholics who wish to seek help, and this is our purpose.

Join us!
name: Everlasting Sobriety

description:
Welcome to The One Family Daily Online OPEN Meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous @ 6:30am PST For 1 Hour.

THIS IS A (STRICTLY) VIDEO MEETING, IF ANYONE'S VIDEO IS TURNED OFF OR NOT SHOWING THEIR FACE ON THE CAMERA, WILL BE REMOVED. 

When we have a Newcomer in the Room, The Meeting Lasts for 90 Minutes.
Join 5 Minutes Early. IF any Zoom Bomber(s) are FOUND, The room Gets Locked.

The Newcomer is the most Important person in the Rooms of AA and we give them a very warm welcome. 
Do Join Us Every Morning.
We Welcome Anyone & Everyone who has a desire to stop drinking.
Topic: Daily Reflections & General Sharing
Court Verifications are Available.
(Note) Verifications will NOT be sent to those who have their video OFF & Not showing their face on the camera.
name: One Family

description:
Come start your day with us; anyone with the desire to stop drinking is welcome.

Breakfast Club is an online fellowship of alcoholics from all over the world practicing the principles of A.A. in all our affairs. Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics to achieve
sobriety.  

We meet at 8:00 AM ET - Everyday of the year!

Monday - Topic Meeting
Tuesday - Big Book Study (slowly)
Wednesday - As Bill Sees It Discussion Meeting
Thursday - Step Study from 12x12. Last Thursday of the month we study the Tradition of the month.
Friday - Story Day (We read a story from that back of the Big Book and discussion follows)
Saturday - Foundation Meeting focusing on Steps 1, 2, & 3
Sunday - Prayer & Meditation focusing on Step 11
name: AA Breakfast Club

description:
Welcome to the Morning Meditation of Alcoholics Anonymous. This is a closed meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. Closed meetings are for AA members or for those who have a drinking problem and have a desire to stop drinking,

In celebration of the autonomy of all A.A. groups, we choose to read from a variety of spiritual publications which we have found to be helpful. The chosen reading becomes the topic of our morning meditation, which is followed by group participation. Our participation is voluntary and ought to be a time for sharing experience, strength, and hope in order to solve our common problem and help others achieve sobriety. Our mission is to carry the message
of Alcoholics Anonymous. Our group purpose is getting through THIS DAY sober.

We meet Sunday-Friday

description:
We meet every Thursday & Friday at 3 pm EST. 
Many of us have questions in early sobriety. We welcome your questions and try to answer them. You can ask them anonymously if you want.

The Zoo Crew Hosts several meetings everyday in the same Zoom room. We have a Movie Matinee Sundays at 2 pm EST. We watch a movie together on Zoom.

We go thru the 12 Steps in 4 hours every month. We have a 2-hour Recovery workshop every month.

Send e-mail to Zoom247AA@gmail.com for a list of all our Meetings and Events.
name: AA Ask It Basket - Sobriety Questions Answered

description:
The purpose of the Primetime AA meeting is to talk about the reason to come to Alcoholics Anonymous;
to expose alcoholism not just as a word, but as a living mind-powered disease; how the disease appears and functions in our lives today in order to
deepen our awareness of what we are up against.

We meet online every Friday night at 8pm EST 5pm PST

The meeting is 1 hour long with a 25 minute speaker - after which we open the floor for sharing.

Visit our website for meeting ID and passcode.
name: Primetime Toronto

description:
Jesteśmy polskojęzyczną grupą AA związaną z ruchem YPAA (Young People in AA, czyli młode osoby w AA) która spotyka się w każdą sobotę o godzinie 18:00 (czasu polskiego).
W czwartą sobotę miesiąca mamy anglojęzyczną spikerkę, która tłumaczona jest na język polski.
Wszystkie pozostałe spotkania będę odbywać się wyłącznie w języku polskim w formacie mityngu spikerskiego, czytania Wielkiej Księgi lub spotkania tematycznego. 
 
Zapraszamy wszystkich!

We are a Polish-speaking YPAA group that meets each Saturday at 6pm (CET).
The 4th Saturday of the month we have an English-speaking speaker translated to Polish.
All other weekly meetings will be conducted only in Polish in the format of speaker meeting, Big Book study or discussion meeting. 
No password required, waiting room enabled

Everybody is welcome!
name: Y.A.S.S. (Young Adults Staying Sober)

description:
"Once a pickle, you can never become a cucumber again."
We invite every recovering alcoholic to this meeting! All you need is a desire to stop drinking.

We have alternating hosts who choose their own topics, they choose readings from the AA Big Book and/or 12&12, the grapevine or anything relating to recovery and addiction. Please come and share your experience, strength and hope with us! Or, just come and listen!
name: AA is a Big Dill

description:
SisTx is a closed women’s meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous that is limited to persons who have a desire to stop drinking.

Our group hosts solution-based meetings focused on studying the AA Big Book, the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions (12 & 12), and other AA Conference-approved literature, along with guided discussion topics.


Meets daily at 9:00 AM, 12:00 PM, 6:00 PM, and 8:00 PM (Central Standard Time).
name: Sisters in Sobriety Texas - 6 PM Women's Closed Meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous

description: We are a women only group of Alcoholics Anonymous and we adhere to the Traditions to the best of our ability, particularly that of primary purpose (#5: We have but one primary purpose—to carry the AA message to the woman alcoholic who still suffers.) and we have no outside affiliation(#6: Our group does not endorse, finance, or lend the AA name to any related facility, or outside enterprise, so that problems of money, property and prestige will not divert us from our primary purpose).  Our Women's only meeting is a closed meeting for women members only, or for those women who have a drinking problem and "have a desire to stop drinking."  The group focuses on reading and discussions based on AA approved literature - Daily Reflections.https://www.goodbeginningsgroup.com/Meeting ID:858 7095 8873PW:Password 488314
name: Good Beginnings Women's Group of Alcoholics Anonymous

description: The Sunday Morning Gay Men’s Stag group is committed to the specific needs of gay men in recovery, but in the tradition of AA, is open to all who wish to attend.  We meet weekly on Sundays via Zoom at 9:30am - 10:30am (PST).  The Online meeting supplements our In-Person meeting, which meets at the Castro Country Club on 18th Street in San Francisco's Castro neighborhood at this same time.  The Sunday Morning Gay Men’s Stag meeting alternates between a speaker-discussion and an open-discussion meeting on alternate Sundays.  We welcome gay men in recovery from all areas around the globe.
name: Sunday Morning Gay Men's Stag - Online

All our meetings are password protected. Please email us for the password

description:
We meet Monday through Saturday from 9:45 am to 11:00 am EST with women only fellowship 15 minutes before and 15 minutes after the meeting.

On Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays we read from “A Woman's Way Through the 12 Steps” Book and Workbook & “Drop the Rock”. 
On Tuesdays and Thursdays, we read from the Big Book 
( http://www.portlandeyeopener.com/AA-BigBook-4th-Edition.pdf ).  
On Saturdays, it’s Chairperson’s Choice with topics such as speakers, alcohol recovery related literature, writing/art exercises, etc.

We share all texts on the screen for those that do not have their own copy of the book. Each member is allotted 3 minutes for shares, with a gentle reminder when they have 30 seconds remaining. We encourage double and triple dipping in this meeting, time permitting.
name: AA Zoo Crew22 - A Safe Place for Sisters in Sobriety

( http://www.portlandeyeopener.com/AA-BigBook-4th-Edition.pdf ).  
On Saturdays, it’s Chairperson’s Choice with topics such as speakers, alcohol recovery related literature, writing/art exercises, etc.

We share all texts on the screen for those that do not have their own copy of the book. Each member is allotted 3 minutes for shares, with a gentle reminder when they have 30 seconds remaining. We encourage double and triple dipping in this meeting, time permitting.

description:
We welcome everyone from across the country and all around the world! Pull up a chair and join us for a "Mocktail" and come experience a unique music meeting where we can still have a good time WITHOUT Alcohol!

Here's the format for this meeting: 
We play songs that have had a positive effect on our recovery and then share about them. Come in up to 15 minutes before the meeting and send your song request to the DJ. We ask that the person bringing the song limit their sharing about the song to just a few short minutes. We try to play lyric versions of the songs during the regular, two-hour meeting period. And then after the meeting, many members choose to stay and keep playing more varied songs and videos in a more casual, “fellowship” environment for up to an additional hour and a half. If you love music, friendship and recovery, please come check it out!
name: AA Zoo Crew22 - After Hours in The Zoo (Stay Tuned to Sobriety)

description:
The Morning Zoo meets 7 days a week at 8:15 am EST. Beginners and old-timers are Welcome! We are now open 24 hours 7 days a week! Put us on while getting ready for work. We help you kick off your day on a bright and fun note and make your morning commute a little better.

We are Not a Glum Lot!
The Morning Zoo Daily Themes:
Monday – Crazy Hat Day (Minnie Pearl Day)
Tuesday – Tiara Tuesday
Wednesday – Western Wear
Thursday – Bring your Pet to the meeting
Friday – Wear Pink (Think Pink, Don’t Drink)

The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors! Originated out of the USA but we are International. We are going on another Sober Cruise later this year. More Sober Adventures are coming in 2024. Join us!

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.”

Mon thru Sat: We read the Daily Reflections & How it Works
Sunday: Speaker Meeting

Monthly Workshops: The 12 Steps in 2 hours. Also a 1-hour Recovery Workshop. 

Come get a Virtual White, Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip and tell us how many days/months/years you have! Get a 1-Minute Chip! Everyone's time is important!

Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. Watch our training video: https://youtu.be/5ivUO0PK3j8 and E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com

description:
Beggars, Tramps & Queers is an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous that meets 7 days a week at 8:30 pm ET. 
We welcome anyone with a desire to stop drinking, including LGBTQIA+ and allies. 
And, we take care to respect diverse opinions about the practice and interpretation of AA principles. All our meetings allow time for discussion.

Sunday – Living Sober
Monday – Glad Day Affirmations
Tuesday - Soundtrack for Sobriety
Wednesday – Wednesday’s Wheel of Sobriety
Thursday – Literature for Recovery
Friday – Agnostic Sobriety
Saturday - Newcomer Meeting

description:
The meeting is set on the fictional 'recovery island' and founded on AA principles and traditions with an open and friendly atmosphere where all alcoholics feel safe to come and share.  The meeting comprises of main shares, general group sharing, meditation, spiritual sections, Recovery tools, big book discussions and social events.

We take the friendly and empathetic approach and welcome all alcoholics with a desire to stop drinking.  Whilst we focus on alcohol, we are also an addict friendly meeting as we understand many alcoholics have had problems with other substances.  Alcohol after all is a drug.  We recognize such people have a wealth of experience, strength and hope which can be of great benefit to others.
Monday- Main Speaker Meeting
Sunday.- 'Serenity on Sunday'
name: Desert Island Recovery

description:
We meet each Friday at 3:30 pm EST. 

It is possible to NEVER have a bad day in sobriety, just bad moments. It's all in the mindset. 
We remember moments, not days. Even if 23 hours, 59 mins and 59 secs are bad it doesn't have to be a bad day because of your Higher Power and the 12 Steps.  
Open Discussion.

We celebrated 2 years on Zoom in March of 2022. 

The OZ (Original Zoo) Crew Hosts a 2-hour Recovery Workshop monthly. We also go through the 12 Steps in 4 Hours monthly.
name: Bad Moments in Sobriety, Never a Bad Day (OZ-Original Zoo Crew)

description:
We meet each Thursday at 3:30 pm EST. 

You don't have to drink No Matter What! There are members of AA who don't drink even after losing a family member (which includes pets). If your butt falls off you put it in a Gucci bag and bring it to a meeting!

The ability to resist that first sucker drink comes thru your Higher Power, the 12 Steps and your own efforts.

We celebrated 2 years on Zoom in March of 2022. 

The OZ (Original Zoo) Crew Hosts a 2-hour Recovery Workshop monthly. We also go through the 12 Steps in 4 Hours monthly.
name: AA No Matter What Club (OZ-Original Zoo Crew)

description:
Join us and see how a mix of Music and Sobriety can go hand in hand on the road of happy destiny!  

We have 8 meetings 7 days a week. We will keep our room open at least 24 hours for all the major Holidays! Info on the website.

Our music meetings are:  
Wed - 3:30 pm EST
Fri/Sat - 7 pm EST

Come see how we the Zoo Crew makes sobriety fun. You'll meet people counting days and those counting years and decades. Everyone's time is important!  We have a great time without alcohol! Bring a song that had a positive effect on your recovery. We'll play the song and then have an Open Discussion. This is still within the AA Traditions and we focus on Recovery.  We are not a glum lot!

Join us every month when we go through the 12 Steps in 4 Hours. We have a 1-hour Recovery Workshop every month. Dates on our website.

Come get a Virtual Chip and tell us how many days/months/years you have! How about a Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip? Everyone's time is important!

Join our Service Team. E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com. We'll train you.
name: 5 O'clock Somewhere - Music and Sobriety (OZ-Original Zoo Crew)

description:
Focus on the Solution from Alcoholism.

Everyone is welcome to attend, especially Newcomers.

This is an Online / Zoom meeting following the traditions and principles of Alcoholics Anonymous.

Our group's meetings are AA Topic Lead share. Lead share for up to 10 minutes.

On the first Friday of every month is a tradition study. The tradition study is the tradition of the month that we are in.

Meeting from the Oregon Coast.. We are International on Zoom.

We do send attendance verification for attending.

Group Conscience Business meeting is Last Saturday following the regular meeting.

We need your help with our meeting! If you are looking for some service to do join us.

We are always looking for Home Group Members!

description:
The Larchmont Beginner's Group Meeting (Closed – Beginners)
🕕 Mondays | 6:00 PM – 7:00 PM CST
📍 Online via Zoom
🔒 Closed Meeting – For those with a desire to stop drinking
"This is a small, supportive meeting designed especially for beginners in recovery. Each week, one speaker shares their experience, strength, and hope — focusing on their experience of what their life was like, what happened, and how it is now in sobriety. 
The second half of the meeting is open for group participants to respond, share, or ask questions related to the speaker's story. There is no pressure to talk if you do not wish to share. 
With 10–20 participants, this meeting offers an intimate and welcoming space for newcomers to listen, engage, and begin building connections in the fellowship."
name: Larchmont Beginners Group

description:
We are the Women’s Early Risers Group of Alcoholics Anonymous. We are a closed meeting, except on Saturdays and the 4th Sunday of the Month when we celebrate Anniversaries we are an OPEN meeting.

Monday: Big Book Study
Tuesday: Daily Reflections begins with 5 minute silent meditation 
Wednesday: Chair's Choice: The chairperson will choose an AA approved topic for today's meeting.
Thursday: Beginners meeting discussion. After speaker, the shares start in this order: 
0-30 days sobriety | 31-60 days sobriety | 61-90 days sobriety
91-6 months sobriety | 6 -9 months sobriety | less than one year | 
Anyone can share.
Friday: Step Series
Saturday: Speaker Discussion (OPEN Meeting)
Sunday: Book series

* We celebrate Anniversaries on the 4th Sunday of the month. Anniversary Celebrations are also OPEN Meetings
No passcode required.
name: Women’s Early Risers

description:
Agnostics in Progress meets Tuesdays at noon PST.  
Anyone with a desire to stop drinking is welcome, believer or not! 

We share our stories and the ways we have made progress in the program.  In this meeting you are free to speak your truth.

Our only wish is to assure you that anyone may achieve recovery in AA without having to deny their own beliefs.

We are here to lift each other up and find strength in the fellowship.  We seek progress, not perfection.
name: Agnostics In Progress

description:
In this meeting we read and go over the steps in the books of Alcoholics Anonymous and the Twelve and Twelve in order. Each week is a new step.  We want to encourage everyone to read along, take notes and highlight those important reminders or suggestions to help you further on your Journey through Sobriety.  Ask Questions or Share your Experience, Strength and Hope with us on what we read and studied today so we all can learn something together.  No passcode required. 
We meet every Saturday afternoon from 3 PM - 4 PM EST. This room is open 15 minutes before the meeting and remains open 15 minutes after the meeting ends for fellowship. Please keep an eye on the chat for important group information.
name: AA ZooCrew22 - Big Book Step Study

Whether you have 1 minute, 1 day, years of sobriety, or just want to find out what A.A. can do for you, we are here for you! Come join us as we recover together!!
name: 4Sobriety

Meets on Tuesday mornings at 11:00 am Pacific time.

As Bill Sees It – Men’s Group, Davis, CA

description: On Awakening is a daily, closed women's 11th step meeting with a focus on meditation and journaling. The format of this meeting is that we read a few brief excerpts related to Step 11 from the Big Book and 12 & 12, then have eleven minutes of silence to meditate & journal. After the period of mediation, people may share their journal entries and/or thoughts as they relate to the 11th step or recovery from alcoholism.
name: On Awakening

description:
Grupo tradicional de AA con mayoría de miembros de Nuevo Leon México. Tenemos juntas ordinarias diariamente.
Dia         Tema
Lun        Capitulos
Mar        Pasos
Mie        Estudio
Jue        Tradiciones
Vie        Compartimiento/P
Sab        Folletos
Dom    Libros
AUTONOMIA:
- No grabar videos, imágenes, ni audios para cuidar el anonimato.
- Mantener el micrófono apagado. Evitar ruido y otros oyentes al rededor.
- Al activar la cámara estar presentable y mostrar solo el rostro.
- Encender la cámara al escuchar y participar para fortalecer la identificación.
- Para usar tribuna se requieren mas de 24 hrs sin consumir alcohol, ni otras drogas.
- No dirigir terapia y usar un lenguaje moderado.
- El tiempo en tribuna será de 10 minutos, a criterio del coordinador.
name: UNIDOS EN LA ADVERSIDAD

description:
Are you sick and tired of being sick and tired?  Do you long to stop the endless cycle of hangovers, loneliness, pain, and despair?  At A Fresh Cup of AA  you will find a group of people who care, who understand your fears and have been where you are now. We aim to help you find hope again.

Our meetings focus on AA’s primary purpose: to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety. We welcome all people. Love and tolerance is our code.

Our rotating format offers:

Sunday – Speaker Meeting

Monday – Beginner’s Meeting for All

Tuesday – Big Book Study

Wednesday –The 12 Steps Study

Thursday – Topic Meeting

Friday – Living Sober with Daily Reflection

Saturday – Grapevine Meeting
name: A Fresh Cup of AA

description: A daily Zoom meeting that shares experience, strength, and hope in the A.A. recovery program to help the still suffering alcoholic. We practice all of the AA Traditions and encourage members to find a sponsor and practice AA's 12 steps to recovery. A speaker shares a personal experience or reads from AA literature and suggests a topic for discussion. On Fridays and Sundays, the speaker talks for 15 to 20 minutes, otherwise 7 to 10 minutes.

We meet 7 days a week at 7 pm EST for a Topic Discussion. Beginners & Old-Timers are welcome along with everyone in between. Come get your mind right! Join the Original Zoo Crew community. Come hear the message of Sobriety and Hope! We are not a glum lot!

We'll help you get a free Big Book if you can't afford it.

The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors! Originated out of the USA but we are International.

We went on 2 Sober Cruises in 2023. Two more Sober Cruises are on the schedule. More Sober Adventures are coming in 2024. Join us!

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as
absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.”

We meet 7 days a week:
Mon & Tues: We read the Daily Reflections & How it Works)
Wed: Drop the Rock (Sandy B. Video) Steps 6 & 7 (Character Defects)
Thurs: Living Sober (Will answer many questions newcomers have about
sobriety.) For example: Can I go to a party? Can I keep liquor in the
house? What about relationships and sex? How about drinking dreams?
Why can't I sleep? Is it okay that I'm craving a lot of sweets?
Fri: It’s 5 O’clock Somewhere (Music & Sobriety)
Sat: Drop the Rock Book - Steps 6 & 7 (Character Defects)
Sun: Speaker Meeting

Monthly Workshops: The 12 Steps in 2 hours. The 12 Steps in 4 hours (You actually take the 12 Steps). Also a 1-hour Recovery Workshop. 

Stay for the Chips at the end of meeting, it will blow your mind! Come get a Virtual White, Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip and tell us how many days/months/years you have! Get a 1-Minute Chip! Everyone's time is important!

Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. We will train you. Watch our training

description:
We will explain the A.A. program to you, give you a newcomers packet, recommend you come to five meetings in a row. We will give you suggestions on detoxing, AA literature to read and get you started on the First step. We will take you through the steps and  sponsor you. . All you have to do is keep coming back and try not to drink between meetings. For people coming back (Slippers) we'll help you get started again. Workshop means we will guide through  the steps and Books.

We began in March of 2020 as Clean Livers online, the online version of an in person meeting by the same name which had been running for over 30 years. We decided on a name change since so many new people showed up.

Waiting Room

description:
This daily meeting was started by members of the Southside Group in Tucson, AZ who moved away, but wanted to stay connected and continue to carry the message of sobriety to newcomers nationwide. We strongly recommend sponsorship, meetings, and working the 12 steps. We love AA and are grateful for sobriety.

Each night we also have a "Meeting after the meeting", where we invite newcomers to ask questions and get phone numbers and maybe get a sponsor, and it also provides fellowship for all members. *NEWCOMERS ENCOURAGED TO ATTEND*
name: Southside Nationwide Meeting

description:
AA Visionaries Meets Every Day, (7 Days a Week) at 7pm PST/ 9pm CST/ 10pm EST.

*Come and share your vision of experience, strength and hope with this casual crew! Visionaries is an Open Meeting, Welcome to all lengths of sobriety from newcomers to old timers…We have a Tradition of The Month and super cool new format for every day of the week. 
EACH NIGHT WE MEET TO GAIN A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF ONLY AA APPROVED LITERATURE.

Monday - Tradition Night (12 & 12 or Illustrated Traditions)
• Tuesday- Big Book Study - 1st 164 Pages
• Wednesday- Living Sober
• Thursday- Stories from the Back of the Big Book
• Friday - STEP Night (12&12)
• Saturday- GAME NIGHT! Daily Reflections Spin Wheel
• Sunday- Illustrated Concepts

***After the meeting we do have a parking lot for fellowship. Our Group Conscience meets the First Friday of Every Month after the meeting . Come Share your Vision of What Sobriety is like for you!
name: AA Visionaries

*Come and share your vision of experience, strength and hope with this casual crew! Visionaries is an Open Meeting, Welcome to all lengths of sobriety from newcomers to old timers…We have a Tradition of The Month and super cool new format for every day of the week. 
EACH NIGHT WE MEET TO GAIN A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF ONLY AA APPROVED LITERATURE.

Monday - Tradition Night (12 & 12 or Illustrated Traditions)
• Tuesday- Big Book Study - 1st 164 Pages
• Wednesday- Living Sober
• Thursday- Stories from the Back of the Big Book
• Friday - STEP Night (12&12)
• Saturday- GAME NIGHT! Daily Reflections Spin Wheel
• Sunday- Illustrated Concepts

***After the meeting we do have a parking lot for fellowship. Our Group Conscience meets the First Friday of Every Month after the meeting . Come Share your Vision of What Sobriety is like for you!
name: AA Visionaries

description:
We read small sections of the book 12 Steps and 12 Traditions and have a lead share on the reading. We then open the meeting to group discussion on the weekly topic. Free online copies of the 12x12 can be found here: https://www.aa.org/pages/en_US/twelve-steps-and-twelve-traditions

Closed meeting. We abide by the 12 Traditions and ask attendees to not take screenshots or recording of any kind. We do not sign court slips or offer proof of attendance.
name: 1 Page at a time 12x12 Saturday (1DAAT)

description:
This is a secular AA meeting where everyone is welcome. From our preamble: "This group endeavors to maintain a tradition of free expression, and conduct a meeting where alcoholics may feel free to express any doubts or disbeliefs they may have, and to share their own personal form of spiritual experience, their search for it, or their rejection of it. In keeping with AA tradition, we do not endorse or oppose any form of religion or atheism. Our only wish is to ensure suffering alcoholics that they can find sobriety in AA without having to accept anyone else's beliefs, or having to deny their own." Please join us!

Meeting is from 8-9pm CT.
The room is open from 7:30-9:30pm CT for fellowship

To dial in: Find your local number: https://zoom.us/u/abbOkgcWoE
name: Atheist & Agnostic

description:

4th Thurs: a reading from any AA literature; 5th, Speaker’s choice).
