description:
Day Openers Group meets at 7 am 365 days a year in Wallingford, CT at the Renaissance Club, a 12 step-based recovery club 501(c)3 supported solely by recovery membership and meetings.  

We are a Big Book based meeting every morning at 7 am. 
Sunday As Bill Sees It, 
Monday Daily Reflections, 
Tuesday 12 and 12, 
Wednesday Gratitude-meditation read from BB, ABSI, or any AA approved literature, 
Thursday 12 and 12, 
Friday 24 hour Book, 
Saturday Big Book Step Study: "I LOVE THIS STEP" Meeting
-We are a solution based group “Sobriety—the freedom from alcohol—through the teaching and practicing of the twelve steps is the sole purpose of an AA group.”
The purpose of this meeting is to help alcoholics achieve sobriety by the studying, discussing, and practicing of the twelve steps as they are laid out in the Big Book.
It has been our hard-learned experience that other methods did not work with us. Some of us have tried other methods and our results were disastrous until we looked at the basic and simple approach the Big Book offers."

description:
We meet at 12 am Eastern / 9 pm Pacific, 7 Days a Week.
We begin the meeting with a 3-5 minute guided meditation, followed by the 11th Step Prayer, and read the When We Retire at Night paragraph on Page 86.  We then have sharing until we close with another 3-5 meditation and a prayer.
The Meeting is 60 Minutes every night except Wednesday and Saturday. Wednesday we have a 45 minute meditation in the beginning of the meeting and our meeting is extended to 90 minutes.  Saturday Night meeting is a 75 minute meeting and is a Speaker/Discussion meeting
name: When We Retire At Night

description:
Our group was started by Key Westers at the very beginning of the pandemic. Today our attendees are from all over the
US, Canada and even globally. KW 12 Noon Group is an English-speaking, closed meeting featuring both audio and video for individuals who have a desire to stop drinking. We abide by the 12 Traditions and ask attendees to refrain from taking screenshots or recordings of any kind. Our group has its own website, providing home group information, a link for attendance verification and more. Our group service positions rotate monthly at our business meeting, and volunteering is encouraged.

Our weekly formats are as follows:

Monday: Chairperson chooses topic from AA approved literature
Tuesday: Chairperson chooses topic from the 12 & 12
Wednesday: Chairperson chooses topic from AA approved literature
Thursday: 25-minute speaker meeting, followed by group discussion
Friday: The 4th dimension and Spiritual Experiences
Saturday: Beginners' meeting; Newcomers share for the first half hour
Sunday: 45-minute speaker meeting

As people who normally would not mix, when we lost our legs and were unable to grow new ones, even we were shocked at our seeming worldliness and levity. But just underneath all of that there is deadly earnestness. We found that God is everything or nothing. Possibly obscured by calamity, pomp or false idol worship, we've learned that within all of us is the fundamental idea of God. Fooling no one, faith works twenty-four hours a day. It is a power greater than ourselves. The miraculous demonstrations of that power in our lives, are facts older than every one of us. As we are granted serenity, we learn to accept the limits of our humanness, the gift of courage to face life's challenges, and the wisdom to know the difference. All of this is done, one day at a time.
name: Key West 12 Noon Group

As we are granted serenity, we learn to accept the limits of our humanness, the gift of courage to face life's challenges, and the wisdom to know the difference. All of this is done, one day at a time.

description:
Long Beach, CA based group of Alcoholics Anonymous who are online every Sunday from 6-7 PM Pacific time. This meeting is a safe place, and you are welcome to just listen if you do not feel comfortable sharing. We read AA conference-approved literature and share our thoughts and experiences about the literature and sobriety - currently rotating Living Sober, Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions, and the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous. Newcomers are welcome,. We are an open meeting, which means anyone can attend who is interested in learning about the program of AA.. We request that you enter with camera on if possible as this adds to the feeling of fellowship. We provide verification of meeting attendance if you need this for court or other confirmation. 

 Waiting room enabled.
name: AA Literature Study Group Pearls Before Swine 2
Online 12 Step Recovery Where and When Group

description:
AAAmigosAA group es un cibergrupo de Alcohólicos Anónimos formado por alcohólicos de diferentes países y residencias, que utilizamos como lengua el español y celebramos sesiones permanentes en él ciberespacio por la vía del correo electrónico. 
 
Quienes participamos en este Grupo, enfatizamos el espíritu de las Tradiciones de AA, aceptando como único requisito para pertenecer, el deseo sincero de querer dejar de beber, esforzarnos en mantener la sobriedad. Y que nuestro propósito primordial como grupo, es llevar nuestro mensaje al alcohólico que esta sufriendo. 
 
Nuestra sesión de AAA, es cerrada. Nuestras reuniones siguen un formato fijo. El Coordinador de Juntas escoge un compañero para que comparta sobre un tema, mismo que será comentado en él grupo durante una semana. 
 
Todos nuestros temas son basados en la literatura aprobada de Alcohólicos Anónimos.
name: AAAmigosAA

The Attitude Adjustment Group provides a virtual A.A meeting room every Mon-Sat at 7:30am CST for us to come together and safely share our experience, strength and hope with one another so that we may stay sober and help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety. 
If you have a desire to stop drinking, you are very welcome to join us!

Our daily meeting formats: 
 - Monday: Speaker's Choice (AA Literature) discussion
 - Tuesday: As Bill Sees It
 - Wednesday: Women's Meeting
 - Thursday: 12 and 12 Book discussion
 - Friday: Grapevine discussion
 - Saturday: Big Book Study
name: Attitude Adjustment Group

-Miércoles de 8:00-9:30pm con el formato de lectura de las historias del Libro Azul
-Viernes de 8:00pm-9:30pm con el formato de una reunión de oradores.

description:
The Never Alone Again is a one hour Speaker/Discussion meeting open to anyone with the desire to stop drinking.  Originally born out of downtown Boston meetings, we now welcome members from all across the world. The virtual discussion room is open 15 minutes before and after the meeting for fellowship.


Please visit our website for details about the meeting, links to other meetings and to sign up as a speaker (90 days sobriety requested). We would love to hear from you.

Originally born out of downtown Boston meetings, we now welcome members from all across the world. The virtual discussion room is open 15 minutes before and after the meeting for fellowship.


Please visit our website for details about the meeting, links to other meetings and to sign up as a speaker (90 days sobriety requested). We would love to hear from you.
name: Never Alone Again

We are an Open online meeting that is an extension of the “After Hours Group” at the Oasis Club in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida. We meet every week on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Wednesdays.

description:
Rebellion Dogs is a daily closed men's AA meeting limited to those who have a desire to stop drinking.  The group holds a closed literature meeting on Zoom every day from 12 noon to 1 PM Eastern time. We open each meeting with a reading from conference-approved literature.  

To join the meeting please click on the blue zoom button or go to the meeting website by clicking on the website button e or email us for the link by clicking on the email button - rebelliondogs7@gmail.com

description:
We meet every day to stay sober and to facilitate the daily maintenance of our spiritual condition.

Please join us at 6:00 AM (U.S. Pacific)/ 9:00 AM (U.S. Eastern).

Monday Beginner Meeting - we invite a member of AA to share for 15 minutes on Step 1, 2, or 3 (rotation)

Tuesday Topic Meeting – we discuss topics suggested by our members

Wednesday Speaker Meeting – we invite a member of our homegroup to share their story for 15-30 minutes, followed by a sharing session

Thursday Big Book Meeting – we read and discuss pages xxv - 164 of the book Alcoholics Anonymous

Friday As Bill Sees It Meeting – we read and discuss sections from the book As Bill Sees It: The A.A. Way of Life

Saturday Step/Tradition Meeting – we read and discuss the AA book Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions

Sunday Speaker Meeting – we invite a member of AA to share their story for 30-45 minutes

Sunday Anniversary Meeting (the last Sunday of the month) – we celebrate sober anniversaries
name: Global Eye Opener

description:
Sober Stogies is a closed, rather unconventional online discussion meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. We meet weekly on Wednesday at 11pm and Sunday at Noon - all times EST on zoom.
 
What makes us unconventional is our unanimous love for sobriety, spiritual progress and living in our common solution -- all while smoking fine cigars! If you're not a cigar lover, we hope you'll grab a seat in the non-smoking section and join us anyway. We of Sober Stogies are ALWAYS eager to share our experience, strength and hope with smokers and non-smokers alike!
name: Sober Stogies

description:
Most days we read from a daily spiritual/12 step book and use that for a topic, other days someone might want to talk about something else. We will read the preamble and say the serenity prayer together then have a volunteer read the steps, the traditions and at the end we will say the lords prayer or whatever is appropriate together. We do our best to run a safe supportive meeting so that anyone needing fellowship will feel welcome. We usually hang out after for fellowship.

We do confirmations via announcement during the meeting

Most days we read from a daily spiritual/12 step book and use that for a topic, other days someone might want to talk about something else. We will read the preamble and say the serenity prayer together then have a volunteer read the steps, the traditions and at the end we will say the lords prayer or whatever is appropriate together. We do our best to run a safe supportive meeting so that anyone needing fellowship will feel welcome. We usually hang out after for fellowship.

We do confirmations via announcement during the meeting

description:

The meeting splits into a Step and Tradition meeting out of the 12&12, and a Big Book study "down the hall".  Nueva Luz y Esperanza is a group of Spanish speaking anonymous alcoholics whose main objective is to provide a service for all alcoholics who cannot attend face-to-face meetings for reasons of health, work or remote location.

description:
Our Beginner's Literature and Step Meeting is 7 days a week at 5 pm EST. Come jumpstart your recovery and get your mind right.

The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020.  When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors!

We are going on a Sober Cruise in May of 2023. Join us.

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.” Come get your mind right for sobriety!

(BB pg. 24) "At a certain point in the drinking of every alcoholic, he passes into a state where the most powerful desire to stop drinking is of absolutely no avail." There is a solution and it's in the literature and the 12 Steps.

Sun - Living Sober (Will answer many questions newcomers have about sobriety.) For example: Can I go to a party? Can I keep liquor in the house? What about sex? What about drinking dreams?

Mon/Wed - Steps 1, 2, 3 & 10, 11, 12 (Stop doing the 1, 2, 3 shuffle. Start living in Steps 10, 11 & 12 while you do Steps 1 thru 9!)

Tues - Drop the Rock (Find out about our Character Defects. Letting go of what's weighing us down emotionally and mentally.)

Thurs - Big Book Study (We read and discuss the BB line by line to pg. 164.)

Fri - Beginner's Step Meeting (We cover Steps 1 thru 12 in order. A different step each week.)

Sat - Big Book Stories (We listen to and discuss a BB story each week)

Join us every month as we go thru the 12 Steps in 4 hours on Zoom. We also have a 1-hour Recovery Workshop every month. Our other workshops are now on Podcast. 

Come get Virtual Chips and tell us how many days/months/years you have! How about a Zoo Crew Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip? Everyone's time is important!

Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. We will train you. E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com
name: A Check-Up from the Neck UP (Get Your Mind Right)

description:
We meet 7 days a week at 3:30 pm EST for Topic Discussion. Beginners and Old-timers are welcome! Come jumpstart your recovery and get our mind right. We make sobriety FUN!
Originated out of the USA but we are International. We are now open 24 hours 7 days a week!

The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors! Originated out of the USA but we are International. We went on two Sober Cruises in 2023. More sober adventures in the future! Join us!

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.” Come get your mind right for sobriety!

Sat/Sun: Check-Up From the Neck Up (Get Your Mind Right) 
Mon: Ask it Basket (Ask Questions Anonymously)
Tues: Steps 4, 5, 8 & 9 Made Simple (Start Working on the Real Problem)
Wed/Thurs: No Matter What Club - We Don’t Drink No Matter What
Friday: Bad Moments, Never a Bad Day in Sobriety.

Monthly Workshops: The 12 Steps in 2 hours based on the Back to Basics principle. Another workshop where you actually take the 12 Steps in about 4 hours based on the Clarence Snyder "Big Book Sponsorship."

Stay for the Chips at the end of the meeting. It will blow your mind! 
Come get a Virtual White, Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip and tell us how many days/months/years you have! Get a 1-Minute Chip! Everyone's time is important!
name: A Check-Up from the Neck UP (Get Your Mind Right)

description:
Daily online meetings in Dubai organized by the No Half Measures Homegroup. This is an Open Meeting for alcoholics and their family and friends.

As our singleness of purpose, the No Half Measures Homegroup, as stated in our Preamble, is for members to share their experience, strength and hope with each other, that they may solve their common problem and help others to recover from alcoholism.

Our meetings are considered voting groups where we follow the Traditions outlined by Alcoholics Anonymous to the best of our abilities.

Sunday - 164 pages of the Big Book
Monday - Traditions from the 12 & 12
Tuesday - Wheel of Topics
Wednesday - Living Sober Meeting
Thursday - Speaker Share - "As Bill Sees It"
Friday - Steps from the 12 & 12
Saturday - Stories of the Big Book
name: No Half Measures Homegroup Daily Meeting (Dubai)

description:
The Women's Friendship Zoom was established in the Tampa Bay area during Covid; and has remained on Zoom even though some have returned to the live room, because the meeting grew to include women outside the Tampa Bay area, and 'snowbirds' that live halftime in Tampa or just decided to participate remotely.  It is an open discussion meeting with a speaker meeting the 1st Friday of each month.  

Our Mission statement: We want everyone to feel comfortable sharing whatever she wants to share.  At the same time, we want to keep our discussions focused on solutions to problems, rather than the problems themselves.  We ask that all keep the basics of AA, the steps and principles and the spiritual solutions alive in our discussions.

The meeting is open 15 minutes prior to start. Please join the meeting prior to start to identify yourself as a woman in recovery. Participants will not be accepted past 10:30 EST so Zoom bombers do not disrupt the meeting after the start.
name: Women's Friendship

description:
We meet 7 days a week at 11:30 am EST for a Topic Discussion. Take your lunch with us and get your mind right! We make sobriety FUN!

Originated out of the USA but we are International. We are now open 24 hours 7 days a week! The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors! Originated out of the USA but we are International. We've gone on two Sober Cruise already. More Sober Adventures are coming! Join us!

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.” Come get your mind right for sobriety!

M: Big Book Study

T: A Check-up From the Neck Up - Get Your Mind Right

W: Ask it Basket (Ask Questions Anonymously)

Th: No Matter What Club - We Don't Drink No Matter What

Fri: Steps 4, 5, 8 & 9 Made Simple (Start Working on the Real Problem)

Sat: Prayer & Meditation Made Simple (Learn to meditate today)

Sun: Bad Moments, Never a Bad Day in Sobriety

Monthly Workshops: The 12 Steps in 2 hours based on the Back to Basics principle. Another workshop where you actually take the 12 Steps in about 4 hours based on the Clarence Snyder "Big Book  Sponsorship."
Also 1-hour Recovery Workshops. Info is on our website

Come get a Virtual White, Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip and tell us how many days/months/years you have! Get a 1-Minute Chip! Everyone's time is important! Stay till the end for the Chips, it will blow your mind!

Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. Watch our training video:
https://youtu.be/5ivUO0PK3j8 and E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com

name: Back Porch Men's Meeting

description:
A daily online support Zoom meeting with readings & open discussion from The Daily Reflection, AA Big Book, & more. We are not a glum lot. Grounded in the Steps & Traditions of AA, we share our Experience, Strength & Hope with Newcomers & Old Timers alike.

Tradition #3 in Alcoholics Anonymous states, "The only requirement for membership is the desire to stop drinking." Open to all; everyone is welcome to attend. Meets daily from 7:00 AM to 8:00 AM USA EST. If you want to get sober or if you’re feeling tempted, talk with us. If you just want to listen in, come on in.

description:
We meet 7 days a week at 7 am EST. Come get your mind right! Put us on while you're getting ready for work or getting the kids ready. We make your mornings brighter!

Originated out of the USA but we are International. We are now open 24 hours 7 days a week! The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors! We are going on another Sober Cruise later this year. More Sober Adventures are coming in 2024. Join us!

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.” Come get your mind right for sobriety!

M/T: Check-Up From the Neck Up
W: Steps 1, 2, 3 & 10, 11 & 12 (Stop the 1, 2, 3 Shuffle)
Th/F: Don’t Drink No Matter What Club
Sat: Prayer & Meditation Made Simple
Sun: Speaker Meeting

Monthly Workshops: The 12 Steps in 2 hours based on the Back to Basics principle. Another workshop where you actually take the 12 Steps in about 4 hours based on the Clarence Snyder "Big Book Sponsorship."
Also a 1-hour Recovery Workshop. 

Come get a Virtual White, Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip and tell us how many days/months/years you have! Get a 1-Minute Chip! Everyone's time is important!

Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. Watch our training video: https://youtu.be/5ivUO0PK3j8 and E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com

description:
An open discussion meeting focused on newcomers to AA, in an open, compassionate setting. Sometimes raw, always honest. Through fellowship, we learn from each other every day as we share experiences, lean on each others strength and move forward, together, in hope.

11am Eastern. every morning
8pm Eastern, every evening. Here’s our evening schedule:

Monday – Open discussion
Tuesday – Open discussion
Wednesday – Open discussion
Thursday – Big Book Study and Step Study in alternating weeks
Friday – Open discussion
Saturday – Soulful Saturday or open discussion, Chair’s Choice
Sunday – Open discussion

You are not alone – our group is accepting, nonjudgmental, and compassionate…we get it, because we’ve been there, too. From all walks of life, and with a broad range of Sobriety dates, ranging from days to decades, we found a place of healing and safety. And it’s open to all.

description:
This is a secular meeting of AA in which we endeavor to maintain a tradition of free expression, and conduct a meeting where alcoholics may feel free to express any doubts or disbeliefs they may have, and to share their own personal form of spiritual experience, their search for it, or their rejection of it. 

In keeping with AA tradition, we do not endorse or oppose any form of religion, agnosticism or atheism. Our only wish is to reassure suffering alcoholics that they can find sobriety in AA without having to accept anyone else's beliefs, or having to deny their own. 

We want this to be a familiar, safe and loving space where all people who have any problems with alcohol will feel welcome, cared for and nurtured.
name: AA Costa Blanca Secular Meeting

We love you - Keep coming back! 🫶💖

name: Kittery Original Group: Online

description: An online only meeting that started as a step study using the Big Book.  It has grown into a weekly literature meeting wherein we explore the basic text of Alcoholics Anonymous, the personal stories located in the back, the role they play in our recovery, and where we can find ourselves in its pages.  We meet weekly on Thursdays at 7:00 PM EST  No passcode required.

description:
This is the men’s meeting for the AA group Sober Stogies. Sober Stogies is a rather unconventional online discussion meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous.
The Sober Stogies Men’s Meeting is held weekly on Mondays at 9pm ET using Zoom video.
What makes us unconventional is our unanimous love for sobriety, spiritual progress and living in our common solution -- all while smoking fine cigars! If you're not a cigar lover, we hope you'll join us anyway. No passcode required.

Sober Stogies also meet as an open meeting on Tuesday at 9PM EST, Wednesday 11PM EST, Thursday 9PM EST, and Sunday Noon EST. Our Women's meeting is Saturday 10AM EST
name: A Sober Stogies Men's

description:
We meet 7 days a week at 6:15 pm EST. We also have a Sober Sisters’ meeting at 10 am EST 7 days a week.

Originated out of the USA but we are International. We are now open 24 hours 7 days a week! The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors!

We are going on another Sober Cruise later this year. More Sober Adventures are coming in 2024. Join us!

Mon thru Sat - Daily Reflections
Sun - Speaker Meeting

The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors!

Monthly Workshops: The 12 Steps in 2 hours based on the Back to Basics principle. Another workshop where you actually take the 12 Steps in about 4 hours based on the Clarence Snyder "Big Book Sponsorship." 

Come get a Virtual White, Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip and tell us how many days/months/years you have! Get a 1-Minute Chip!
Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. Watch our training video: https://youtu.be/5ivUO0PK3j8 and E-

description:
We meet 7 days a week at 6 am EST. Get the Early Bird Special with the Original Zoo Crew! Come get your mind right for the day!

The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors!

We are based in the USA but we are truly international. Our first meeting is at 6 am EST and the last one finishes at midnight with fellowship into the late morning. We are open over 24 hours for all the drinking holidays and the major
holidays. You NEVER have to be alone!

We are going on a Sober Cruise in May of 2023. Join us.

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.”

M/T/W - On Awakening & Daily Reflections
Th/F - No Matter What (We don't drink)
Sat/Sun - Check-up from the Neck Up (Get your mind right)

Join us every month as we go thru the 12 Steps in 2 hours on Zoom. Come to our 12 Traditions Workshop every 2 months.

We also have a 1-hour Recovery Workshop every month. Our other workshops are now on Podcast. 

Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. We will train you. E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com

We are based in the USA but we are truly international. Our first meeting is at 6 am EST and the last one finishes at midnight with fellowship into the late morning. We are open over 24 hours for all the drinking holidays and the major
holidays. You NEVER have to be alone!

We are going on a Sober Cruise in May of 2023. Join us.

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.”

M/T/W - On Awakening & Daily Reflections
Th/F - No Matter What (We don't drink)
Sat/Sun - Check-up from the Neck Up (Get your mind right)

Join us every month as we go thru the 12 Steps in 2 hours on Zoom. Come to our 12 Traditions Workshop every 2 months.

We also have a 1-hour Recovery Workshop every month. Our other workshops are now on Podcast. 

Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. We will train you. E-mail: Zoom247AA@gmail.com

description:
We're an open meeting devoted to discussion and practice of the 11th Step: "Sought through prayer and meditation to improve our conscious contact with God as we understood God, praying only for knowledge of God's will for us and the power to carry that out." 

Each week a speaker shares their experience of prayer, meditation, self-inventory, and other steps or measures they take to maintain their spiritual tradition. The lead is followed by 10-15 minutes of guided nondenominational meditation. The last 30 minutes of the meeting are devoted to open sharing.

We meet Thursdays from 7-8 PM EST. 
The meeting is locked during the meditation.
name: AA Into the Mystic

Fridays are topic meetings.

Saturdays start with group mediation followed by sharing.

description:
We meet for a Topic Discussion 7 days a week at 1 pm EST. We offer a safe place where you will not be judged, shamed or shunned.

Join us if you are Neurodivergent also. Join our great online sobriety community!

Newcomers & old-timers are welcome! Anyone with a desire to stop drinking is welcome in the Rainbow Room! Embrace Diversity!

We are totally focused on the solution and carrying the message of HOPE! The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. When the
world shut down during the pandemic, we opened our Virtual Doors!  We are online from 6 am to Midnight and beyond 7 days a week.

Alcoholism centers in the mind. It is cunning, baffling and powerful and unless the obsession to drink is removed we are defenseless against that first sucker drink. (BB pg. 37) “Our behavior is as absurd and incomprehensible with respect to the first drink as that of an individual with a passion, say, for jay-walking.” Come get your mind right for sobriety!

Come get Virtual Chips and tell us how many days/months/years you have! How about a Zoo Crew Pink Cloud or Rule 62 Chip? Everyone's time is important!
name: A Check-up From the Neck Up LGBTQ & More Meeting (aka The Rainbow Room)

We have a meeting at the same time each day, everyday.
ALL meetings are at 5 PM PST

We are women who lift each other up by sharing, supporting and listening. Thankful for our sobriety everyday, we would love to share it with you. Experience, Strength, Hope!

description:
We are an Open Meeting on zoom dating from March 2020. We meet 7 nights a week at 9pm Pacific time. Our format is for the leader to pick a portion from the first 164 pages of the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous. On Fridays we read a whole story from the back of our book.
We each read a few paragraphs and pass to the next person. We read until 9:30pm, except on Fridays. We then go around and share about what we have just read. We often run past the hour so that everyone has a chance to share. 

Newcomers and Long timers are welcome. We usually stay after for fellowship and to answer questions.
name: Mission Hills Late Night/A Vision for You Group

description:
The HEAL room is dedicated to those who wish to focus on the Spiritual aspect of their recovery. 

We have claimed this space to give voice to people, and to share and identify with others in this AA 12 step room as double winners, healers, energy workers, lightworkers, spiritually gifted, highly sensitive, empaths and intuitives, mediums, mystics, psychics, and more. This is by no means an exhaustive list of how our loving HP ’s, Goddess’ or Gods’ may express themselves in our meetings, our lives, our healing, and our continued recoveries. Our primary purpose is to carry the message to the alcoholic who still suffers.
name: The Heal Room

description:
Speaker gives brief description of coming to AA with or without relapses.  Then focuses on their first two years of recovery, utilizing or not utilizing the tools of recovery suggested to them. Then first year people share on same topics. Then second year people share on same topics.  With time remaining rest of the meeting share on the same topics.  

Waiting Room is enabled, All will be admitted by Host or Co-Host.  All participants are muted upon entry.  Meeting is not recorded.  Chat is open throughout the meeting.  We remain online 15 minutes after the close for questions and general talk.

12 Steps, 12 Traditions and 12 Concepts derived from the AA Big Book.

name: Living The Big Book Meeting

description:
A one-hour Tuesday morning women's & non-binary meeting. 

We start with reading the "Upon Awakening" passage from the Big Book and either have a speaker or do a suggested topic/open share. Discussion is done 'pitch style,' where the first sharer will pick the next sharer, etc. 

The last 15 minutes of the meeting will be raise-of-hands, rather than pitch. 
This meeting is a very open and welcoming space. 
We welcome the discussion of drugs & other addictions, difficulty with the God-concept, etc. 
We meet a 6am PT (9am ET).
name: Broad Highway

description:
The Strange Paradox Meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous started in 2020 in Pinellas County, Florida and meets Sunday through Saturday at 12:00PM EST.

We have attendees from Florida and many other states and countries.

Our name reflects the many strange paradoxes found and experienced in AA such as "Surrender to win" - "You have to give it away to keep it" - "The gift of Despair."

We are a small discussion group with a mix of new and seasoned members, and have lively discussions of topics and issues.

Everyone is welcome and we are very supportive of newcomers.

Sunday: Gratitude / Discussion Meeting

Monday: Tom’s Ask it Basket / Topic Meeting

Tuesday: As Bill Sees It

Wednesday: Daily Reflections

Thursday: Steps and Traditions

Friday: Big Book Meeting

Saturday: Speaker / Discussion Meeting
name: Strange Paradox

description:
Welcome home! We aim to foster a fun, loving, and safe environment focused on recovery from alcoholism.

We are an open meeting and adhere to the 12 traditions. Our primary purpose is to carry AA’s message to the alcoholic who still suffers.

We meet 7 days a week at 5:00EST

Meeting topic is reading from the Daily Reflection and sharing on that or any topic pertaining to your sobriety. Chairperson rotates daily. Shares are not timed and the meeting continues past the hour until all with their hand raised have the chance to share.

We keep the room open before and after for fellowship and support for as long as needed. Attendance verification provided. Students and observers are welcome. We do open the meeting 30 minutes prior to.
name: A New Spiritual Family

description:
Sisters of Serenity (SOS) – Closed Online AA Meeting
Mondays at 7:00 PM Eastern

Join us each Monday evening for connection, reflection, and inspiration. This is a closed Alcoholics Anonymous meeting for women only — focused on living and learning the AA program.

Weekly Schedule of Topics:
1st Monday: "Voices of Women in AA" – Guided reading & reflection
2nd Monday: 11th Step Meditation – Quiet your mind, connect with your higher power
3rd Monday: Emotional Sobriety – Tools for staying centered and grounded
4th Monday: Guest Speaker Night – Experience, strength, and hope from a fellow woman in recovery
5th Monday: Open Discussion – Share what’s on your heart

Meeting Details:
Meeting begins promptly at 7:00 PM Eastern.
Please introduce yourself with video on before we start.
The room is locked at the start of our meditation or discussion to avoid distraction.
Limited to 25 participants.

Join us: visit https://aawv13.com/meetings/zoom.html for the current link.

Questions? Email online@aawv13.com

We look forward to meeting you!
name: Sisters of Serenity

description:
Love Across the Universe (LATU) is an international group that hosts five online meetings a week.

This is an OPEN meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous and all are welcome. We ask that only those with a desire to stop drinking or using share at this meeting as it relates to your experience, strength and hope for recovery.

This is a tag participation meeting with the leader sharing for 10 minutes and selecting a topic for discussion. The first 10 minutes of sharing are reserved for newcomers with ‘tag’ sharing afterwards. You are free to listen and pass if called on.

We meet weekly on Mondays at 7PM BST
name: Love Across The Universe Topic Tag Participation Meeting

description:
Love Across the Universe (LATU) is an international group that hosts five online meetings a week. 

This is an OPEN meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous and all are welcome.
We ask that only those with a desire to stop drinking or using share at this meeting as it relates to the reading and your experience, strength and hope for recovery. 
'All You Need Is Love' is a weekly discussion of the stories from the back of the Big Book. We pick up the story where we left off from the previous week.

Meeting format: A volunteer reads a few paragraphs and the meeting opens for sharing. Once everyone has had an opportunity to share, we continue reading and sharing as often as time allows. 
Participants are always welcome to just listen.

We meet Fridays weekly at 7PM GMT
name: All You Need Is Love

description:
Strong sobriety with a Sedona vibe. Gather with our eclectic community at 7:00 a.m. Arizona time (Mountain Standard Time) on Sundays, Mondays, and Fridays. 

We read from Daily Reflections, As Bill Sees It, the Big Book, and other recovery literature, then share our experience, strength, and hope. 
On Sundays we start with a meditation followed by lots of healthy discussion. 
Join us from wherever you are as we hike the trail of happy destiny.

Sunday - 11th Step meditation, open discussion
Monday - Daily Reflections, open discussion
Wednesday - Topic meeting, open discussion
Friday - As Bill Sees It, open discussion

All meetings start at 7:00 a.m. Mountain Standard Time (AZ).

description:
Welcome to the Slow Learners' Group. We set this up for ourselves, for our sponsees, and for their sponsees to keep current with our spiritual growth. It is open to any AA member.

We're PIGS: People Interested in Growing Spiritually.

We're also HOGS: Helping Others Grow Spiritually.

Most importantly, we're Slow Learners (and Faster Forgetters).

We cover and re-cover the Twelve Steps, the Twelve Traditions, and the Twelve Concepts, and in covering and re-covering these, we, ourselves, recover from a seemingly hopeless state of mind and body.  
No passcode required
name: Slow Learners AA Group Friday

description:
At Rocketeers, you “BYOT” (bring your own topic)!  We go around the room. Each member introduces themselves and their own topic. The Chair then randomly calls on members to share on their own topic, followed by random members to share on that member’s topic. Anything from “Acceptance” to “Favorite sober snacks”! We usually get to 4-6 topics per meeting! Diverse topics! Fun and insightful meeting!  
No passcode required.

description:
Welcome home! We aim to foster a fun, loving, and safe environment focused on recovery from alcoholism. We are an open meeting supporting newcomers specially those in their first 90 days through the AA program. Our primary purpose is to stay sober & carry AA’s message to the suffering alcoholics around the world.

We are here 7 Days a Week…

Mondays - Speaker Meeting
Tuesdays - Daily Reflection
Wednesdays – Speaker Meeting
Thursdays – Speaker Meeting
Fridays - 12&12, Steps & Traditions
Saturday – Topic Meeting
Sunday – Speaker Meeting

We offer home group membership to get involved into service & enjoy our fellowship, support & sponsorship, open shares, attendance verification, and meeting after the meeting. Our Daily meeting is a great tool to build connections & know more about AA.

We are here Daily at 9:00PM UK, 4:00PM EST, 1:00PM PST. The room will be opened 15 minutes before the meeting to welcome you and allow us to know you more.

This is a WE program, and it works if we work it.
name: AA Newcomers International

description:
This is an open women’s meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous and our group is focused on emotional sobriety! In this group we read and discuss stories from the Grapevine book, The Next Frontier: Emotional Sobriety.

I think that many oldsters who have put our AA “booze cure” to serve but successful test still find they often lack emotional sobriety. Perhaps they will be the spearhead for the next major development in A.A. – the development of much more read maturity and blanche (which is to say, humility) in our relations with ourselves, with our fellow and with God.  Welcome to Women in Emotional Sobriety!

Last Tuesday of the month is a hybrid meeting with the original WIES meeting for our birthday celebration.
name: Women In Emotional Sobriety

description: Somos um grupo de Alcoólicos Anónimos Online, cujo o objectivo é levar a Mensagem e o Programa de Recuperação de AA aos alcoólicos que não têm ou não podem participar em reuniões presenciais nos seus locais de residência em Portugal Continental e Ilhas (Madeira e Açores), bem como àqueles que estão imigrados em outros países. We celebrate anniversaries on the last Sunday of the month. 
We welcome all with open arms.

We meet Monday - Sunday at 7am Eastern Standard Time

description:

We invite every recovering alcoholic to this meeting! All you need is a desire to stop drinking.

We have alternating hosts who choose their own topics, they choose readings from the AA Big Book and/or 12&12, the grapevine or anything relating to recovery and addiction. Please come and share your experience, strength and hope with us! Or, just come and listen!

description: The purpose of the Seniors in Sobriety International meetings is to provide a forum for seniors to celebrate and maintain their sobriety, to discuss challenges and solutions for recovery facing seniors in their golden years, and to encourage participation by members of all ages to bring A.A. to seniors who suffer from alcoholism later in life.

description:

Each participant is called on to read one paragraph in turn. (Anyone may opt out of reading aloud.) For the second half of the meeting we share our personal experiences and perspectives in relation to the readings.

The Zoom session starts one half hour before the meeting formally begins.

PLEASE TURN ON VIDEO MOMENTARILY AFTER INITIAL ENTRY.

description:
Welcome to Liberty Path Workshops! Do you need a Sponsor? Do you have questions about Steps 1-5? You are you in the right place! We meet every Saturday for 5 hours to help you through the first 5 Steps! We
start off by covering "The Doctor’s Opinion" and "Bill’s Story". Then we move onto "How It Works" before writing out our personal inventories together - don’t worry, we’ll walk you through it! description:
Welcome home! We aim to foster a fun, loving, and safe environment focused on recovery from alcoholism. We are an open meeting supporting newcomers specially those in their first 90 days through the AA program. Our primary purpose is to stay sober & carry AA’s message to the suffering alcoholics around the world.

We are here 7 Days a Week…

Mondays - Speaker Meeting
Tuesdays - Daily Reflection
Wednesdays – Speaker Meeting
Thursdays – Speaker Meeting
Fridays - 12&12, Steps & Traditions
Saturday – Topic Meeting
Sunday – Speaker Meeting

We offer home group membership to get involved into service & enjoy our fellowship, support & sponsorship, open shares, attendance verification, and meeting after the meeting. Our Daily meeting is a great tool to build connections & know more about AA.

We are here Daily at 9:00PM UK, 4:00PM EST, 1:00PM PST. The room will be opened 15 minutes before the meeting to welcome you and allow us to know you more.

This is a WE program, and it works if we work it.
name: AA Newcomers International

description:
This is an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. We meet every Sunday at 9AM Eastern Time on Zoom for one hour and we believe the world gets better with every new person who meditates and improves their conscious contact with God. We practice Step 11 as suggested in the 12 and 12 and the Big Book. The same script is read each week, although not necessarily by the same person, and it rolls for about 45 minutes. There are three segments to our meeting… a guided meditation, a silent meditation, and a short segment for sharing towards the end of the meeting.

Please email the group at ConsciousMeditationAA@gmail.com for the passcode prior to the 9am EST meeting start time.
name: Conscious Contact Beginners Meditation Meeting

description:
This is an open women's meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
Anyone interested in our program of recovery may attend this meeting. 
We read the first 164 pages of the Big Book. We read a few pages at each meeting. 
On the last Saturday of the month, we read one of the women’s stories in the back of the Book. The reading is followed by a short lead. 
If you’d like to share on the topic, you may raise your virtual hand and we’ll call on you in the order received. 
We keep our comments to about 3 minutes and focus on the common solution to alcoholism.
name: A New Chapter - Women's Big Book Journey

description:
We are a roomy, all-inclusive, never exclusive meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous.  We meet 7 nights a week at 5:30pm PST// 8:30pm EST. Our format varies depending on the day of the week from open discussion to tradition studies and newcomer meetings.  Though originating out of Las Vegas, we started out with homegroup members from NV to NC. We share experience, strength and hope from East to West US Coasts, and would absolutely love to hear stories from
across the globe!  We have a Virtual Chip System and would love to celebrate milestones with you! (Monthly up to a year, 18 months, yearly).   We look forward to hearing all of your stories- your experience, strength and hope!
name: Only A Symptom

Topic Meeting for GAY MEN approaching and over 40.  In the spirit of the Third Tradition all are welcome.

The focus at HJF-/+40 is to discuss the ways we stay sober while growing older. Members talk about solving problems using the tools of the AA program, our gratitude for living in the present, and the joys we find in sober living.

FOR SECURITY, we ask that you send an email to: happy.joyous.free.nyc@gmail.com to ask for our password.  We will be happy to add you to our mailing list.

HJF also has an in-person Meeting in NYC, Mondays at 6:30.

Join us!!!
name: Happy Joyous & Free - Gay Men Approaching and Over 40

description: This is a 7pm EST Topic/Discussion AA Group that meets in Hampton, VA every Thursday for 1hr. This is a HYBRID meeting, there will be a live meeting as well as Zoom participants who can share their ESH on the topics presented or on any other AA related topic.
name: Ft Monroe Group - Topic/Discussion Meeting

description:
Presentación:
Ofrecemos un camino hacia la sobriedad en Alcohólicos Anónimos sin dogmas religiosos, deidades, poderes superiores o rituales.
Somos un grupo de AA que respeta la libre expresión, donde puedes compartir tus dudas, experiencias espirituales personales o rechazo a conceptos espirituales.
No respaldamos ni nos oponemos a ninguna forma de religión o ateísmo.
Nuestro único propósito es asegurar a las/los alcohólicas/alcohólicos que sufren que puedan encontrar la sobriedad en AA sin tener que aceptar las creencias de nadie más o tener que negar las propias.

¿Ｃóｍｏ Ｆｕｎｃｉｏｎａｍｏｓ？
En nuestras reuniones, compartimos experiencia, fortaleza y esperanza desde una perspectiva secular.
Trabajamos juntos para resolver nuestro problema común y ayudar a otros/otras a recuperarse del alcoholismo.
La cámara y la participación son opcionales. Respetamos el anonimato, base de todas nuestras tradiciones.

Ｉｎｃｌｕｓｉｖｉｄａｄ
El único requisito para ser miembro de AA es el deseo de dejar la bebida.
Todas las personas son bienvenidas, sin importar su etnia, género, orientación sexual, sistema de pensamiento, religión, nivel de ingresos o profesión.

Nuestro espacio está diseñado para personas que desean dejar de beber que se identifican como ateas, agnósticas o librepensadoras.
Ofrecemos un lugar seguro, libre de todo tipo de acoso, donde puedes sentirte apoyado/apoyada.
________________________________________
Únete a nosotros en este viaje de recuperación desde una perspectiva secular. ¡No estás sola/sola!

Ｃｏｎｔáｃｔａｎｏｓ：aajimburwell@gmail.com

description:
The Sandpiper Group of Alcoholics Anonymous was founded in 1978 by four women who emphasized the Steps, Traditions, Concepts, Big Book, 12 and 12, Sponsorship, and Service. This closed women's meeting continues this legacy online in a discussion format and invites you to join us. Newcomers welcome!

To ensure a safe space, the zoom waiting room will close at 10 minutes after the meeting begins. We ask participants turn on their video upon entry. You may turn it off afterward, if you wish. No avatar videos, please.
name: Discussion Meeting for Women – The Sandpiper Founders' Group of AA

description:
A place where people can share in a smaller setting, where we can study, discuss and hear others sharing their experience, strength, and hope from reading through the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions.

"We sit in A.A. meetings and listen, not only to receive something ourselves, but to give the reassurance and support which our presence can bring." - 12 & 12, Step Twelve.

Come join us in studying the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions. We look forward to seeing you!
name: 319 12 Steps and 12 Traditions Meeting

description:
Taller de 12 Pasos de Alcohólicos Anónimos para ateos y agnósticos.

Durante este taller de una hora y 30 minutos, revisaremos los 12 Pasos de Alcohólicos Anónimos desde la perspectiva de Glenn Rader, página por página.

Nuestro objetivo es leer y explorar los 12 Pasos con una discusión continua centrada en los principios y valores del programa de recuperación de Alcohólicos Anónimos; y esclarecer dudas e inquietudes
y/o su experiencia hasta el momento con los pasos.

Bienvenida cualquier persona que desee dejar de beber, sin importar su raza, género, orientación sexual, religión, nivel de ingresos o profesión.
La cámara y tu participación es opcional, el anonimato es la base de todas nuestras tradiciones.
name: A.A. Ateos y Agnósticos en Español

description:
Our purpose: The members of this group are committed to practicing the 12 steps as outlined in the “Big Book” of Alcoholics Anonymous. It is our intent to share our experience, strength and hope with those who
suffer from the disease of alcoholism so that we may carry out A.A.’s primary purpose and help alcoholics recover through the 12 steps.

This group uses a different meeting format each week of the month.
name: BBA Central

description:
The Seeking Serenity group hosts a rotating topic meeting every Friday on Zoom! 
Enjoy readings from the 12 Steps and 12 Traditions, As Bill Sees It, The Daily Reflections, and a speaker every month!

Meets every Friday from 8PM to 9PM.

description:
We are a new Zoom meeting of AA for LGBTQ+ folks and their allies, based in Reykjavik, Iceland. 
This is an open meeting that meets every Saturday at 7 PM GMT (Iceland time)
This is a speaker discussion meeting 3 Saturdays out of 4. 
We have 1 Random format meeting on the the first Saturday of the month.

We look forward to seeing you!
name: The Northern Lights LGBTQ+ Group of AA

description: Pimlico London “Keep it Simple” is a weekly AA zoom meeting with an invited chair/speaker, focusing on “keep it simple”everyone is welcome to attend. The Meeting opens every Tuesday at 12.45 pm starting at 1pm, GMT UK time duration “1hour” In the recovery world, “Keep It Simple” has been a familiar phrase since Alcoholics Anonymous began in 1939. It was the favorite phrase of Dr. Bob, one of the cofounders of AA. During his last speech at the national AA convention in 1950, he spoke of the simplicity of the AA solution.
name: Pimlico Keep It Simple Online meeting

description:
1 hour meeting using zoom platform bi- weekly Tuesday reading from the Big Book, with discussion
Thursday Step meeting. Reading from the 12 n 12 with discussion.
name: Sunrise Solution

description:
Hello and Welcome to SOS!

We, here at SOS, like to offer a safe place for women to continue to recover together. We come from all walks of life and choose to engage in love, patience and tolerance as we trudge. To another day being sober!

Sisters of Serenity Meetings

Sunday 8am EST (5am PST) On Awakening

Monday 1pm EST (10am PST) Grapevine stories

Tuesday 6pm EST (3pm PST) Emotional Sobriety The Next Frontier

Wednesday 2pm EST (11am PST) 12&12

Thursday 3pm EST (12pm PST) Big Book 164

Thursday 7pm EST (4Pm PST) Discussion

Friday 6pm EST (3pm PST) Book study

Saturday 8am EST (5am PST) On Awakening

Steps for attendance verification:

1. Please have your video on throughout the meeting

2. During the meeting send the chairperson a message in the chat,
informing her that you are looking for verification during the
meeting.

3. Soon after the meeting, send an email to
SistersOfSerenitySOS@gmail.com with your name and what meeting
attended for verification. One of the admins will respond to your
request in a timely manner.

Thank you, we look forward to Trudging the Road of Happy Destiny with you

-Sisters of Serenity-

description:
AAAmigosAA group es un cibergrupo de Alcohólicos Anónimos formado por alcohólicos de diferentes países y residencias, que utilizamos como lengua el español y celebramos sesiones permanentes en él ciberespacio por la vía del correo electrónico. 
 
Quienes participamos en este Grupo, enfatizamos el espíritu de las Tradiciones de AA, aceptando como único requisito para pertenecer, el deseo sincero de querer dejar de beber, esforzarnos en mantener la sobriedad. Y que nuestro propósito primordial como grupo, es llevar nuestro mensaje al alcohólico que esta sufriendo. 
 
Nuestra sesión de AAA, es cerrada. Nuestras reuniones siguen un formato fijo. El Coordinador de Juntas escoge un compañero para que comparta sobre un tema, mismo que será comentado en él grupo durante una semana. 
 
Todos nuestros temas son basados en la literatura aprobada de Alcohólicos Anónimos.

description:
The No Matter What meeting is a closed meeting for A.A. members only or for those who have a drinking problem and have a desire to stop drinking. It is a place where secular, women and non-binary individuals can find sobriety in AA without having to accept anyone else's beliefs or having to deny their own. We do not endorse or oppose any form of religion, atheism or political affiliation. Our only wish is to ensure suffering alcoholics that they find a supportive and nurturing environment to enhance their sobriety.

The meeting will integrate certain aspects of traditional and secular AA such as the Steps and Traditions. We share our experience, strength and hope to encourage "a design for living" that really works. Starting 12/3/23.
name: No Matter What AA Meeting (Women and Non-Binary)

L-Cubed: Lucan Legacies & Literature is a reading and discussion open AA meeting which focuses on study of the Three Legacies of Unity (12 Traditions), Service (12 Concepts), and Recovery (12 Steps), as well as the AA Big Book and other AA literature.

Week 1: Step of the Month
Week 2: Tradition of the Month
Week 3: Concept of the Month
Week 4: Big Book, First 164
Week 5: Other AA Literature
name: AA L-Cubed: Lucan Legacies & Literature

description: At this meeting we usually read the daily reflection and upon awakening. Then we open the meeting for solution based sharing.

description: At this meeting we take turns to read short sections of the Big Book, and then open the meeting for sharing and discussion.
name: Big Book Reading AA England

description:
West Cork Fellowship (WCF) was started as an online AA meeting in the Spring of 2020. It is now in its fifth year.

Meets Mon, Wed, Fri, Sat 1pm GMT and Wed at 7pm GMT
Monday, 1 pm– Daily Reflections reading & discussion
Wednesday, 1 pm – Topics discussion
Wednesday, 7 pm – Speaker meeting
Friday, 1 pm – Speaker meeting
Saturday, 1 pm – Step & Tradition reading & discussion

WCF has a group conscience meeting approximately every 6 weeks, one week in advance of the West Cork Area meeting.
name: West Cork Fellowship

description:
The name of our group comes from the old AA story of a group that tells about a group that had a lot of rules (61 to be exact!) and wanted to control all aspects of their members. Ultimately they
decided that they only needed one rule, Rule 62 "Don't take yourself too damn seriously"

We feel the same, we're here to stay sober, offer experience, strength, and hope, and have a really good time doing it. We focus on kindness, love, and friendship. If that's something you are into, you're in the right place!
name: Rule 62

description:
Svoboda is an AA beginners group that meets via zoom every Monday at 7:00PM ET
Once a beginner, always a beginner. All are welcome.

If you have a desire to stop drinking, please join us as we share our experience, strength, and hope.
If we are painstaking about this phase of our development, we will be amazed before we are half way through. We are going to know a new
freedom and a new happiness. Svoboda is the Ukrainian word for freedom.
name: A Beginners Meeting at Svoboda

description:
The 9 to5 Online Group is a LGBTQIA+ special interest and friendly group, however ALL are welcome especially the newcomer and US and
Worldwide visitors. Our group meets via Zoom on Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday’s at 6:00pm US MST (Mountain) 

Our primary purpose is to stay sober and to help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety. In accordance with Tradition 5, we ask that all who share confine themselves to the topic of recovery. We have a rotating meeting Chairperson who facilitates the meeting via a meeting script and We have a meeting Moderator who manages the technology, security for all of our meetings.  Group Conscious meeting on the 1st Tuesday of the month and Service positions available for members in all lengths of sobriety

Welcome!

description:
Open Discussion Meeting for women. Newcomers are welcome and encouraged to join us. Old-timers are valued and treasured, too. The only requirement for membership or attendance is a desire to stop drinking. Topics are determined by the volunteer leader of the day.

The last meeting of each month is usually a speaker meeting where those celebrating an AA anniversary can share their stories. This is a very warm and welcoming group based in Asheville, North Carolina.
name: Women of Courage

description:
A Old School Meeting is a weekly Topic Meeting based on Topics taken directly from Approved AA Literature.
Our mission is to stay sober and to help other alcoholics achieve sobriety. 
We are committed to upholding the AA Traditions
name: A Old School Meeting

description:
Join our long-standing meeting based in southern Florida. We are an open meeting with a single speaker, followed by 30 minutes of sharing. We invite newcomers to our meeting, and our meeting is built around the first three steps of AA. We will be open 15 minutes ahead of the meeting time, and will be open for fellowship after the meeting as needed.

A password will be required to attend our meeting. Please email monriverbottom@gmail.com for the password.

Any behavior deemed inappropriate by our host or co-hosts will be met with removal. We ask you to respect the AA process, and we, in turn, will gratefully help you get and stay sober.
name: Monday Night Riverbottom

description:
Young Gunz In Recovery is an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting, but addicts are also welcome. The newcomer is the most important person in this meeting. When necessary, we do first step meetings for newcomers and attendees should come with a welcoming and helpful spirit towards our newcomers.
If a first step meeting is not necessary, we will pick a topic or read from our official AA literature. Our information and topics are straight from official AA literature.
Above all, we are all common people, here in our fellowship, one with the other, no matter your background- one fellow helping the other is what we do.

This is a 2-hour meeting. We meet 7 days a week from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. eastern time (5:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. Mountain Time). All are welcome.
name: Young Gunz In Recovery

description:
Интернациональная группа АА «ИГрАА» проводится ежедневно, в конференц-программе ZOOM, в видеоформате, на русском языке.
АА «ИГрАА» проводит ежедневные закрытые собрания для алкоголиков.

Группа представлена участниками примерно из 20-ти стран Мира, географический охват постоянно раширяется. Благодаря видеосвязи атмосфера на группе приближена к живой встрече.

Начало проведения собрания (ежедневно):
9 a.m. New York Time/USA
15.00 Central European Time
17:00 Москва/Россия

Официальная часть собрания 1 час 30 минут, затем неофициальная часть в формате свободного общения для новых и постоянных участников группы.

Пн., вт., ср., чт, сб.: чтение отрыка книги «Анонимные Алкоголики», «12 шагов 12 традиций», обсуждение по прочитанному и возможность задать дополнительные темы, которые касаются АА и алкоголизма.
Пт и Вс.: спикерские собрания с возможностью задать вопрос спикеру. Иностранным спикерам обеспечивается синхронный перевод на русский
язык.
name: ИГрАА ("IGrAA", "The Game")

name: Carpet Slippers Big Book Study

description:
** FOR THE SAFETY OF THIS MEETING, YOUR VIDEO MUST BE TURNED ON UPON ENTRY!! Once verified by a host/co-host, video may be turned off. If we're unable to verify that you're a real person/alcoholic in the first minute or so of you joining, you will be removed. We have zero tolerance for crude, hateful, offensive disruptions, so if you're joining with these intentions, don't bother... you WILL be removed and reported IMMEDIATELY. If you join late and the meeting is locked, we apologize... this was done in order to ensure the safety of the room and those sharing, so please look for another meeting to join this morning and come back and see us again next Sunday!! Thank you for understanding! **

We are an open, HYBRID meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous, based in the Greater Seattle Area. Our primary purpose is to stay sober and to carry the AA message to the still suffering alcoholic.

We meet every Sunday morning from 9:30–10:30 AM PST to share our experience, strength, and hope (heavy on the hope!). The newcomer is the bloodline of our meeting. We're based in a treatment center, as well as have treatment centers that occasionally join us virtually, so we focus a lot on Steps 1 thru 3, but also discuss other AA related
topics.

FORMAT:
An alcoholic with a year or more shares for the first 5-6 minutes and chooses a topic, then calls on people of their choosing to share until about 10:10am (PST), then they open the meeting up to raised hands, switching between online and in-person participants. We celebrate AA birthdays on the last Sunday of every month. We hope you’ll join us!

In-person Location:
2nd Chance Recovery Center
235 SW 153rd St, Burien WA 98166-2313
name: Sunday Morning Magic

description:
Hello MEN, and welcome to The Dynamic Recovery Group. A 7:15-8:15 pm EST vigorous AA Big Book Study. 
This online zoom meeting is a gathering of men who are seeking recovery from alcoholism through the principles and program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We are a very active group serious about the Big Book.

The Dynamic Recovery Group provides a safe and supportive environment for men to connect with others who are also seeking recovery from alcoholism. With any issues you present, our group process will attempt to direct you to a solution from the Big Book. Our open format allows respectful crosstalk and ongoing feedback during the meeting. We ask that you show respect for others and the group by making this meeting your primary activity.
name: Dynamic Recovery Big Book Study

description:
We are a meeting dedicated to providing an open-minded, safe, care-free and all-inclusive fellowship. 

We are an open meeting of AA which meets Mon-Fri 8:30 AM EST and 9:30 AM EST on Sat-Sun. 
Our fellowship is built on the principles of Unity, Service, Recovery and Doing the next right thing , One day at a time. We welcome Everyone, especially the Newcomer. A strong emphasis on Rule 62 (Don’t take yourself so seriously) is encouraged here.

If you are looking for a meeting that thinks outside the box, JOIN Us!
You too, can become A Clandestine Traveler

description:
We are a festive, loving, safe, and welcoming group. We are open to newcomers and old-timers worldwide. Our focus
is on recovery, and we share our experience, strength, and hope with one another. We practice RULE 62 (Don't take yourself so seriously) and welcome you to join! We currently have seven meetings weekly.

Below are the times and descriptions of each meeting.

This is an open meeting. Students are welcome to attend but we ask that you do not share.

We offer attendance verification as well. Please pay attention to the chat during the meeting for more information on how you can obtain your verification.

AA All Recovery offers chips to those celebrating milestones and anniversaries. Please join us and watch the chat to find out how you can claim your chip. Congratulations on your time and keep coming back.

We hold a monthly group conscience and happily give out service commitments to anyone willing to be of service.

MONDAY (9 am EST): Step 6 & 7 and time for sharing

TUESDAY (9 am EST): Gratitude Meeting (Rule 62) and time for sharing

WEDNESDAY (9 am EST): Recovery Topics and time for sharing

THURSDAY (9 am EST): "Daily Reflection" and time for sharing

FRIDAY (9 am EST): Ask It Basket and time for sharing

SATURDAY (9 am EST): "Plain Language Big Book" and time for sharing

SUNDAY (9 am EST): Music Meeting and time for sharing
name: AA All Recovery

description:
Newcomer-based open and accepting meeting, ALL are welcome.
Rotating format.

First week of the month-Speaker/discussion.
Second week-Big Book
Third week-Living Sober book study
Forth Week-Check-in/Ask It Basket
If Fifth-Daily Reflections.

Waiting room enabled
name: NewTimers AA

description:
The in-person meeting was established over 30 years ago as a "closed" meeting. As a result of the pandemic we started meeting on Zoom. It has continued to serve the folks who for one reason or another can't be at an in person meeting. (The in-person meeting meets at the Sandals church in Lake Arrowhead every  Tuesday). We focus on how to live sober one day at a time by staying in the solution rather than the problem and working the 12 steps as described in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
Our meeting format: we read the Preamble, "More About Alcoholism" and How it Works, The Twelve Traditions and "The Promises" from the Big Book, we share about "what it was like, what happened, and what it's like now"
name: Monday Evening Lake Arrowhead Men's Stag

description: The AA Big Book has touched many lives, it has made possible for many to change and to enjoy a new freedom beyond our imaginations. In this meeting we will read stories, chapters that touch our hearts in many ways. We will have the opportunity to share our individual experiences that relate to what we read, and even share if it did not. This meeting is open to anyone who is interested and has the desire to get and stay sober. Open to anyone, regardless of where you are at, regardless of where you have been, were only interested in where we are all going as a group of Men and Woman who crave and desire a new way of life. The AA Big Book has changed my lives! Let's grow together, and trudge together to the road of Happy destiny.
name: Path to Freedom

description:
We are a group of alcoholics that come together through an open discussion meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. We welcome all persons who have a desire to stop drinking or wish to learn more about alcoholism; outlining a solution which is offered in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous

All meetings begin with: “How it Works” - pg. 58 of the B.B & “On Awakening” - pg. 86 of the B.B.

Monday - Spiritual Awakening (7am MST)
Tuesday - As Bill Sees It (7am MST)
Wednesday - Grapevine (7am MST)
Thursday - Emotional Sobriety (7am MST)
Friday - A.A. Speaker (7am MST)
Saturday - Topic Wheel (7am MST)
Sunday - Living Sober (7am MST)
* all readings are taken from AA approved literature.

We close our meeting with a paragraph taken from pg. 552 of the B.B. “Freedom from Bondage”

We are fully self-supporting through our own contributions. We are not allied with any sect, denomination, politics, organization, or institution. We do not wish to engage in any controversy, neither endorses, nor opposes any causes. Our primary purpose is to stay sober, and to help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety.
name: Good Morning Resentment

Meet us online from any computer, smartphone or tablet. Access via Zoom. Interact with the people at the Elgin location, from anywhere you have internet access.
No Password required, just click on the link and wait until someone let's you in.
In-person:
Kubo
70 S Grove Ave.
Elgin, IL 60120
Convenient location in Downtown Elgin. Come early for fellowship and to help set up. Interact with the people from the online meeting without messing with computers or your phone.

description:

Check out our website for meeting access, resources, and a private community page.

description:
Newcomers welcome and encouraged to attend. 
We do a daily reflection meeting every single day of the week. Monday - Sunday 7:00 am CST, 8:00 am EST. 

Open to all; everyone is welcome to attend. Join us as we read over the daily reflection and discuss what it means to you. Feel free to bring up a topic that you may be struggling with, and we will share our experience, strength, and hope. 

We have a wide range of members, those with a day sobriety all the way to 32+ years. It is a great place to come, and stay sober. We have sponsors who are willing to help you get started on the steps. We gladly give out phone numbers to help you get sober sisters and brothers in your phone. 
You don't have to do this alone.

description:
We are a fun and down to earth meeting with varying lengths of sobriety. 
We meet on zoom in the morning from 06:15-07:15 EST and our format changes daily so we can explore the Big Book, and other AA literature. 
We welcome all to our warming community where you will find support and learn Experience, Strength and Hope from others or from a variety of AA literature.

The Format for the Early Risers is:

Monday: Beginners Meeting
Tuesday: either "Came to Believe" or "Living Sober"
Wednesday: Daily Reflections
Thursday: Big Book Study
Friday: 12 Steps & 12 Traditions
Saturday: Speaker Meeting
Sunday: "As Bill Sees It"

description:
Come join our All Night Why Are You N.U.T.S? International Meeting!
N.U.T.S. is an acronym for Not Using The Steps.

We meet 7 days a week at 6:00 PM, 7:00 PM, 8:15 PM, 1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM, and 6:00 AM EST

Daily: 6:00 AM EST Daily Reflections (Mon - Fri)
Daily: 6:00 PM EST No Matter What Club! (Mon - Sun)
Daily: 7:00 PM EST Big Book Study (Mon - Sun)
Daily: 8:15 PM EST Joe & Charlie Tapes (Mon - Sun)

ROTATING FORMAT BELOW FOR OTHER HOURS

Monday: Steps 6 & 7 (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Tuesday: 12 x 12 Study (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Wednesday: Living Sober (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Thursday: As Bill Sees It (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Friday: Big Book Study (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Sat/Sun: Music and Sobriety (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM, 6:00 AM)

All Inclusive!

If you are an alcoholic (or have a desire to stop drinking) You are Welcome here!

Doors Open Daily at Midnight (12 AM) EST!
name: All Night Why Are You N.U.T.S?

description:
Geeks Who Don’t Drink (GWDD) is an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
GWDD began in the Pacific Northwest, though we welcome those from anywhere, new and old, who have a desire to quit drinking.
GWDD offers an eclectic range of virtual meetings, from book studies and topic discussions to open shares and speaker meetings.

We play music in this meeting and then discuss it. Songs that had a positive impact on your sobriety. Join us for fun and fellowship!

The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. We have picnics around the country for meet and greets. Come join our community.


Join the Zoo Crew Service Team. Watch our training video: https://youtu.be/5ivUO0PK3j8
name: A Checkup From the Neck Up - Music & More Beginner's Meeting

description:
Small group with lots of sobriety. We welcome everyone with a desire to stop drinking especially newcomers. 
Currently we are reading twelve steps and twelve traditions to start off our meeting focused on recovery from alcoholism.
name: Midweek Recovery

description:
This is an online, open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
We have an informal, 60 to 90 minute format starting at Midnight Eastern.

Sometimes we read from the Big Book, 12 & 12, Daily Reflections, Living Sober, or other literature; other days we just focus on honest sharing and frank discussion. 

Cross-talk is allowed; disruption is not. This meeting is a safe safe for everyone and those suffering from cross-addiction are more than welcome!
name: Midnight Serenity

description:
The McCall Back to Basics Noon meeting is an open meeting of Alcoholic Anonymous for anyone interested in the program of recovery from alcoholism. As Tradition 3 states, "the only requirement for A.A. membership is a desire to stop drinking." 
We are a solution-based meeting who meet DAILY at 12:00 PM – 1:00 PM MDT. Our fellowship includes all levels of sobriety, all are welcome especially the newcomer.

description:
Closed meeting meeting 6 nights a week, 1 hour long, varied topics and format on each night.  
We are a registered closed group of Alcoholics Anonymous meeting 6 nights a week Monday to Saturday. 
We follow the 12 steps and 12 tradition. Meetings start from 7.30pm - 8.30pm GMT London. Room open 15 minutes before for fellowship.
Monday - The Promises
Tuesday- Speaker share night
Wednesday- Big Book study
Thursday- Newcomer and main share
Friday- Spin the wheel and topic share 
Saturday- Stories from the Big Book experience strength and hope

First Sunday of every month Women's meditation meeting, Last Sunday of every month Men's meeting - email for details. 

Together we are stronger.
name: Altogether AA

description:
Hello MEN, and welcome to The Dynamic Recovery Group. A 7:15-8:15 pm EST vigorous AA Big Book Study. 
This online zoom meeting is a gathering of men who are seeking recovery from alcoholism through the principles and program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We are a very active group serious about the Big Book.

The Dynamic Recovery Group provides a safe and supportive environment for men to connect with others who are also seeking recovery from alcoholism. With any issues you present, our group process will attempt to direct you to a solution from the Big Book. Our open format allows respectful crosstalk and ongoing feedback during the meeting. We ask that you show respect for others and the group by making this meeting your primary activity.
name: Dynamic Recovery Big Book Study

description:
We are a supportive and welcoming space open to all women of Alcoholics Anonymous. Our meetings provide an opportunity to connect with other women in recovery, share experiences, and find strength in our collective journey. We meet every Thursday night at 8pm EST and our meeting focuses on recovery-related topics and discussions on AA
literature.

Whether you are new to AA or have been a member for years, our group offers a nurturing environment where you can engage in meaningful conversations and find inspiration from fellow members. Come as you are, and let’s support each other on the path to recovery!
name: Lotus Women's Meeting

description:
This group of Alcoholics Anonymous is for anyone who identifies as a Sober Secular Sister. We welcome those who consider themselves free-thinkers, are fully inclusive to those who hold "non-traditional" beliefs concerning their spirituality and a higher power, and support those who seek an alternative approach to their personal recovery
journey.

This group operates in voluntary compliance with all A.A. Traditions.

Questions or attendance verification: sobersecularsisters@gmail.com
name: Wolverine Women's Eye Opener

description:
We meet every Monday, Wednesday and Friday from 1 PM and Sunday 9:30 AM  EST .  
The room is open 15 minutes before and remains open 15 minutes after the meeting ends for fellowship.  
We read from the 24 Hours A Day book and then have an Open Discussion with  3-minute shares
name: AA Zoo Crew22 - Sobriety Brothers

description: A weekly speaker / discussion meeting. Based in Rhode Island.
name: Sunday Go To Meetin'

description:
Go to Any Lengths is a closed meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. All who have a desire to stop drinking are welcome to join us. We meet online every night at 7:30pm ET with a different format each night (based on both AA approved and non-AA approved literature).

In an effort to foster a close connection among meeting attendees, everyone is required to turn on their video and leave it on for the duration of the meeting. Those who do not comply are removed from the meeting. There are no exceptions. 

Please call in if you aren't comfortable turning your camera on. 301-715-7011 and use the meeting ID 853 8775 6917 or simply click on the PHONE button for one touch connection.

We offer fellowship with understanding, support and humor (we are NOT a glum lot). AND, free court verification of attendance.

Newcomers and Old-timers alike are welcome! We are a friendly and supportive group and pay special attention to those in early sobriety and who are just coming back.

We have a different topic every night of the week. Please keep coming back!

description:
If your recovery needs a spark, come and join us here at ARC. The Alcohol Recovery Collective is a friendly and informal open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous whose sole purpose is to help fellow alcoholics stay sober and strives to offer a positive, supportive and uplifting experience for all in attendance.

Meetings take place daily at 9pm UK (4pm EST) for one hour, with 15 minutes of Fellowship before and after the meeting. At ARC we read How it Works and the Daily Reflection and then have an open format discussion with 3 1/2 minute shares and a gentle reminder when you have 30 second left. However your day is going, we offer a safe space and want to hear your share. Please join us as we walk the road of recovery together.
name: ARC - The Alcohol Recovery Collective

However your day is going, we offer a safe space and want to hear your share. Please join us as we walk the road of recovery together.
name: ARC - The Alcohol Recovery Collective

description:
Grupo tradicional de estudio con la mision de proporcionar un espacio seguro y acogedor donde las personas que luchan contra el alcoholismo puedan encontrar apoyo, comprension y las herramientas necesarias para una vida sobria.

Reuniones Diarias de 7:30 a 9:00 PM | CST - Tiempo del Centro de Mexico

Lunes : Libro Grande
Martes : Llegamos a Creer
Miercoles : Lenguaje del Corazon
Jueves : Tal Como la Ve Bill
Viernes : 12 Pasos
Sabado : Viviendo Sobrio
Domingo : Tradiciones

Formato usual de las reuniones : Lectura breve + Compartimiento 5-10 min por persona (a juicio del coordinador). No exceso de lenguaje soez ni comportamiento disruptivo.

No importa dónde te encuentres, estamos aquí para apoyarte.
name: Viveros Virtual MX

Tuesday, Daily Reflections or Anniversary Meeting

Wednesday, Big Book Meeting read from first 164

Thursday, The Newcomers Nook

Friday, Pass-It-Forward A Big Book Stories Meeting

Saturday, read a chapter from Living Sober,

ODAAT is a group of meetings based in Brighton & Hove UK that transferred to on-line March 2020 after many years face to face.

THURSDAY 19.30 UK - Big Book Study Meeting 90 mins, studying the text week on week for first 30 mins followed by a chair and share-backs
FRIDAY 19.30 UK - Always a Newcomer 90 mins, ESH chair focused on steps 1,2 & 3 followed by share-backs
SUNDAY 19.30 UK - Step Meeting 90 mins, a reading from Big Book followed by a chair on the step relative to the reading followed by share-backs
MONDAY 19.30 UK - Speaker Topic Meeting 90 mins, 35 min speaker chair followed by share-backs
name: Brighton & Hove Global - odAAt group - Always A Newcomer Meeting
