description:
The Strange Paradox Meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous started in 2020 in Pinellas County, Florida and meets Sunday through Saturday at 12:00PM EST.

We have attendees from Florida and many other states and countries.

Our name reflects the many strange paradoxes found and experienced in AA such as "Surrender to win" - "You have to give it away to keep it" - "The gift of Despair."

We are a small discussion group with a mix of new and seasoned members, and have lively discussions of topics and issues.

Everyone is welcome and we are very supportive of newcomers.

Sunday: Gratitude / Discussion Meeting

Monday: Tom’s Ask it Basket / Topic Meeting

Tuesday: As Bill Sees It

Wednesday: Daily Reflections

Thursday: Steps and Traditions

Friday: Big Book Meeting

Saturday: Speaker / Discussion Meeting
name: Strange Paradox

description:
Midday Reflections is a Whitby, Ontario-based closed discussion service meeting held every Tuesday & Thursday from 1-2pm EST.
Anyone, anywhere, who has a desire to stop drinking is welcome to join us as we read through some key AA texts (AA Preamble, How It Works, The 12 Steps, The 12 Traditions, The Promises &; the day's reading from Daily Reflections) followed by a frank and authentic discussion as we reflect on these, and other, aspects of fellowship and sobriety.
name: Midday Reflections

description:
Closed meeting meeting 6 nights a week, 1 hour long, varied topics and format on each night.  
We are a registered closed group of Alcoholics Anonymous meeting 6 nights a week Monday to Saturday. 
We follow the 12 steps and 12 tradition. Meetings start from 7.30pm - 8.30pm GMT London. Room open 15 minutes before for fellowship.
Monday - The Promises
Tuesday- Speaker share night
Wednesday- Big Book study
Thursday- Newcomer and main share
Friday- Spin the wheel and topic share 
Saturday- Stories from the Big Book experience strength and hope

First Sunday of every month Women's meditation meeting, Last Sunday of every month Men's meeting - email for details. 

Together we are stronger.

description:
Welcome to The Isle of Misfits!  We are inclusive, never exclusive – ALL are welcome!  Our meetings are a mixture of book studies and open/topic discussions.  We like to take the time to really break the down readings and ask questions, so we truly understand the literature.  We also seek to understand the reasons behind our behaviors and more importantly to find solutions!   
We meet on M-Sat at 12PM EST and Monday night at 7PMEST.   
Monday – Big Book Study 
Monday PM (7pm EST) – Big Book Study – Personal Stories from the back of the book  
Tuesday – Topic Discussion 
Wednesday – Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions Study 
Thursday – AA Related Book Study  
Friday – Guest Speaker Meeting 
Saturday – AA Related Video Discussion

description:

We embrace all with open arms and offer support to those seeking sobriety on their journey to recovery.
No one is ever turned away; all that's required to participate is the desire to stop drinking.
Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety, and we follow the 12 Traditions of A.A.
Different format each night. Welcome!

description:
We are a one hour AA LGBTQ+ English speaking meeting with home group members from across the globe. Each week we read from the AA Daily Reflections book as a topic guide. 
A speaker starts the meeting for approx. 10-15 minutes, then we have open sharing. 
We meet every Tuesday at 7.30pm (London time). 
We care for member's safety with a waiting room and tech hosts who remove unwelcome guests eg: zoom bombers. We look forward to meeting you.
name: Angel LGBTQ+ Online Meeting

description:
"But when we are willing to place spiritual growth first—then and only then do we have a real chance.” -p.114 of the 12 & 12.

We're a weekly (Weds 10-11pm Eastern) open, English-language, online-only (Zoom) speaker-discussion meeting with a twist.

Our meeting begins with a spin of our Wheel of Topics. Our speaker shares on the Wheel's choice of topic for 15-20 mins before we open for discussion. Anyone who raises their virtual hand may contribute.
All are welcome.

To support everyone's safety, we ask all to refrain from harassment and abuse based on race, color, religion, lack of religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or age.

We hope to see you soon. We saved you a (virtual) seat!
name: A Real Chance

description:

The meeting has a lot of sobriety (I have 38 years).

description:
Welcome to The Isle of Misfits!  We are inclusive, never exclusive – ALL are welcome!  Our meetings are a mixture of book studies and open/topic discussions.  We like to take the time to really break the down readings and ask questions, so we truly understand the literature.  We also seek to understand the reasons behind our behaviors and more importantly to find solutions!   
We meet on M-Sat at 12PM EST and Monday night at 7PMEST.   
Monday – Big Book Study 
Monday PM (7pm EST) – Big Book Study – Personal Stories from the back of the book  
Tuesday – Topic Discussion 
Wednesday – Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions Study 
Thursday – AA Related Book Study  
Friday – Guest Speaker Meeting 
Saturday – AA Related Video Discussion
name: Isle of Misfits

description:
AA Steps Meeting in Melbourne, Australia, offered in a hybrid format to support both in-person and online participants. 
Each series runs for 13 weeks with a new chairperson, focusing on one step per week and culminating in a session on spiritual concepts. The chair leads readings from the Big Book and the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions, provides explanations, and encourages members to share their experience, strength, and hope. This structured yet personal approach helps members deepen their understanding of the steps, creating a supportive environment for recovery accessible to all.

description:
Format of the meeting:
Big Book Study. 1st Sat of the month we read a story from the back of the Big Book. The other 3 weeks we read a 3 to 6 page section from the first 164 pages. After the reading we define words then a speaker shares on the section we read for about 10 min to 15 min. The remaining time of the meeting is open for shares on what was read from the Big Book.
name: In the Book

description:
We are a group of alcoholics that come together through an open discussion meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. We welcome all persons who have a desire to stop drinking or wish to learn more about alcoholism; outlining a solution which is offered in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous

All meetings begin with: “How it Works” - pg. 58 of the B.B & “On Awakening” - pg. 86 of the B.B.

Monday - Spiritual Awakening (7am MST)
Tuesday - As Bill Sees It (7am MST)
Wednesday - Grapevine (7am MST)
Thursday - Emotional Sobriety (7am MST)
Friday - A.A. Speaker (7am MST)
Saturday - Topic Wheel (7am MST)
Sunday - Living Sober (7am MST)
* all readings are taken from AA approved literature.

We close our meeting with a paragraph taken from pg. 552 of the B.B. “Freedom from Bondage”

We are fully self-supporting through our own contributions. We are not allied with any sect, denomination, politics, organization, or institution. We do not wish to engage in any controversy, neither endorses, nor opposes any causes. Our primary purpose is to stay sober, and to help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety.
name: Good Morning Resentment

Sisters of Serenity Meetings

Sunday 8am EST (5am PST) On Awakening

1. Please have your video on throughout the meeting

2. During the meeting send the chairperson a message in the chat,
informing her that you are looking for verification during the
meeting.

3. Soon after the meeting, send an email to
SistersOfSerenitySOS@gmail.com with your name and what meeting
attended for verification. One of the admins will respond to your
request in a timely manner.

Thank you, we look forward to Trudging the Road of Happy Destiny with you

description:
Based in Cleveland, Ohio, this AA agnostic group meets daily at 6pm Eastern. 

We endeavor to maintain a tradition of free expression where alcoholics are safe to express any doubts or disbelief they may have, and to share their own personal form of spiritual experience, their search for it or their rejection of it, without fear of criticism.
This open discussion meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous represents the true spirit of an all-inclusive fellowship, where each member is free to develop their own personal beliefs without having to accept anyone else’s, or having to deny their own.
name: Westside Agnostics

description:
Need a daily dose of serenity? 
There’s really nothing hard about prayer and meditation! 
Come join our AA4L4U family each day for a beautiful way to start or take a break from your day. Each day we offer a reflective reading followed by your personal prayer and meditation for 10 minutes. Participants are encouraged to share their experience, strength and hope as it relates to the day’s reading. The serenity you need is yours for the taking! 

Drop in or make this part of your daily routine. Remember it’s never too early or too late in your recovery to practice this important step. Come on in and get comfortable!
name: AA4L4U - The Great Oasis

name: Living Sober (Online)

description:
Stepping Stones is a closed women's online only meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. We meet every Monday (including Holidays) at 12pm PST. We are a registered group with the General Service Office of Alcoholics Anonymous and we honor A.A.'s Twelve Traditions. We have a mix of sobriety lengths  at our meeting. We welcome newcomers, oldtimers and all women with a desire to stop drinking. We use a variety of formats:

First Monday of the month: Speaker 
Last Monday: Sobriety Milestones/Birthdays plus Topic Discussion
All Other Mondays: Topic Discussion (From the GSO Suggested Topic List or any A.A. published literature)

We have retired women, Moms and working women who come on their lunch hour. We encourage attendees to keep the video on whenever possible and limit distracting activities (walking, driving etc.) Waiting Room secured. Join us!
name: Women's Stepping Stones

description:
Welcome to our open AA meeting. We are a solution-based group focused on recovery through AA literature and the practice of the 12 Steps and 12 Traditions.

For the safety and unity of the group, we ask attendees to join with their cameras on. We understand if you choose to turn your camera off after joining, but we do encourage active participation.

As identifying members of Alcoholics Anonymous, our primary purpose is to help others find recovery through consistent practice of the Steps and Traditions, fostering love, humility, and service in all areas of life.”

8:30 am-10 am est and 8:30 pm-10 pm est Monday-Sunday

On-Line Meeting link above and on website
name: Solution 62

description:
Alcoholics Anonymous Recovery with Challenges (AARC)  is dedicated to providing a welcoming and supportive environment for individuals recovering from alcoholism who also face challenges related to mental and physical health, including trauma and chronic conditions.
We meet every Sunday at 3: 00 EST and Thursday at 9:00 PM EST on Zoom to listen to a speaker share their own story or read a story from AA-approved literature that focuses on our needs. Relevant topics are discussed during the sharing portion of the meeting.
name: Alcoholics Anonymous Recovery with Challenges (AARC)

description:
SPEAKER MEETING
Plaza Group has been doing it since May of 1954. We have both online and in-person meetings centered in Charlotte, NC. This is our online Wednesday meeting. We'd love you to join if you think you have a problem with alcohol, no matter where you are! This is a full speaker meeting, featuring a different AA speaker every week-- sharing experience, strength, and hope about what we were like, what happened, and what we're like now.
name: Plaza Group

description:
A safe place on Monday mornings where women can hear the EXPERIENCE, STRENGTH AND HOPE of other recovered women. Open meeting but smaller and more intimate. Speaker will share openly about their struggles and how they were overcome. Women can find support, encouragement and recovery from the hopeless state of mind and body that kept them drinking. Video must be upon entering meeting.


May God grant us the wisdom and fortitude ever to sustain an unbreakable unity.
name: Sobriety Sisters Turning the Page
Back To Basics Upstate NY / Sober Sisters Saturday

description:
Geeks Who Don’t Drink (GWDD) is an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
GWDD began in the Pacific Northwest, though we welcome those from anywhere, new and old, who have a desire to quit drinking.
GWDD offers an eclectic range of virtual meetings, from book studies and topic discussions to open shares and speaker meetings.
name: Geeks Who Don't Drink - Men's

description:
This AA group is all about diving into the Big Book and the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions. 

We focus on reading, discussing, and sharing what this literature mean to us and how they guide our recovery. We dig deeper into the program, share our experiences, and learn from each other. 

Whether you’re new to AA or have been around for a while, everyone’s welcome. It’s all about connecting, growing, and staying grounded in the principles that help us live a sober and meaningful life.
name: Sunlight of the Spirit Book Study

description:
The Strange Paradox Meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous started in 2020 in Pinellas County, Florida and meets Sunday through Saturday at 12:00PM EST.

We have attendees from Florida and many other states and countries.

Our name reflects the many strange paradoxes found and experienced in AA such as "Surrender to win" - "You have to give it away to keep it" - "The gift of Despair."

We are a small discussion group with a mix of new and seasoned members, and have lively discussions of topics and issues.

Everyone is welcome and we are very supportive of newcomers.

Sunday: Gratitude / Discussion Meeting

Monday: Tom’s Ask it Basket / Topic Meeting

Tuesday: As Bill Sees It

Wednesday: Daily Reflections

Thursday: Steps and Traditions

Friday: Big Book Meeting

Saturday: Speaker / Discussion Meeting
name: Strange Paradox

description:
Presentación:
Ofrecemos un camino hacia la sobriedad en Alcohólicos Anónimos sin dogmas religiosos, deidades, poderes superiores o rituales.
Somos un grupo de AA que respeta la libre expresión, donde puedes compartir tus dudas, experiencias espirituales personales o rechazo a conceptos espirituales.
No respaldamos ni nos oponemos a ninguna forma de religión o ateísmo.
Nuestro único propósito es asegurar a las/los alcohólicas/alcohólicos que sufren que puedan encontrar la sobriedad en AA sin tener que aceptar las creencias de nadie más o tener que negar las propias.

¿Ｃóｍｏ Ｆｕｎｃｉｏｎａｍｏｓ？
En nuestras reuniones, compartimos experiencia, fortaleza y esperanza desde una perspectiva secular.
Trabajamos juntos para resolver nuestro problema común y ayudar a otros/otras a recuperarse del alcoholismo.
La cámara y la participación son opcionales. Respetamos el anonimato, base de todas nuestras tradiciones.

Ｉｎｃｌｕｓｉｖｉｄａｄ
El único requisito para ser miembro de AA es el deseo de dejar la bebida.
Todas las personas son bienvenidas, sin importar su etnia, género, orientación sexual, sistema de pensamiento, religión, nivel de ingresos o profesión.

Nuestro espacio está diseñado para personas que desean dejar de beber que se identifican como ateas, agnósticas o librepensadoras.
Ofrecemos un lugar seguro, libre de todo tipo de acoso, donde puedes sentirte apoyado/apoyada.
________________________________________
Únete a nosotros en este viaje de recuperación desde una perspectiva secular. ¡No estás sola/sola!

Ｃｏｎｔáｃｔａｎｏｓ：aajimburwell@gmail.com

Ofrecemos un camino hacia la sobriedad en Alcohólicos Anónimos sin dogmas religiosos, deidades, poderes superiores o rituales.
Somos un grupo de AA que respeta la libre expresión, donde puedes compartir tus dudas, experiencias espirituales personales o rechazo a conceptos espirituales.
No respaldamos ni nos oponemos a ninguna forma de religión o ateísmo.
Nuestro único propósito es asegurar a las/los alcohólicas/alcohólicos que sufren que puedan encontrar la sobriedad en AA sin tener que aceptar las creencias de nadie más o tener que negar las propias.

¿Ｃóｍｏ Ｆｕｎｃｉｏｎａｍｏｓ？
En nuestras reuniones, compartimos experiencia, fortaleza y esperanza desde una perspectiva secular.
Trabajamos juntos para resolver nuestro problema común y ayudar a otros/otras a recuperarse del alcoholismo.
La cámara y la participación son opcionales. Respetamos el anonimato, base de todas nuestras tradiciones.

Ｉｎｃｌｕｓｉｖｉｄａｄ
El único requisito para ser miembro de AA es el deseo de dejar la bebida.
Todas las personas son bienvenidas, sin importar su etnia, género, orientación sexual, sistema de pensamiento, religión, nivel de ingresos o profesión.

Nuestro espacio está diseñado para personas que desean dejar de beber que se identifican como ateas, agnósticas o librepensadoras.
Ofrecemos un lugar seguro, libre de todo tipo de acoso, donde puedes sentirte apoyado/apoyada.
________________________________________
Únete a nosotros en este viaje de recuperación desde una perspectiva secular. ¡No estás sola/sola!

Ｃｏｎｔáｃｔａｎｏｓ：aajimburwell@gmail.com
name: AA – para Ateos, Agnósticos y Librepensadores

No password required, waiting room enabled.

description:
The Strange Paradox Meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous started in 2020 in Pinellas County, Florida and meets Sunday through Saturday at 12:00PM EST.

We have attendees from Florida and many other states and countries.

Our name reflects the many strange paradoxes found and experienced in AA such as "Surrender to win" - "You have to give it away to keep it" - "The gift of Despair."

We are a small discussion group with a mix of new and seasoned members, and have lively discussions of topics and issues.

Everyone is welcome and we are very supportive of newcomers.

Sunday: Gratitude / Discussion Meeting

Monday: Tom’s Ask it Basket / Topic Meeting

Tuesday: As Bill Sees It

Wednesday: Daily Reflections

Thursday: Steps and Traditions

Friday: Big Book Meeting

Saturday: Speaker / Discussion Meeting
name: Strange Paradox

description:
Welcome to The Isle of Misfits!  We are inclusive, never exclusive – ALL are welcome!  Our meetings are a mixture of book studies and open/topic discussions.  We like to take the time to really break the down readings and ask questions, so we truly understand the literature.  We also seek to understand the reasons behind our behaviors and more importantly to find solutions!   
We meet on M-Sat at 12PM EST and Monday night at 7PMEST.   
Monday – Big Book Study 
Monday PM (7pm EST) – Big Book Study – Personal Stories from the back of the book  
Tuesday – Topic Discussion 
Wednesday – Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions Study 
Thursday – AA Related Book Study  
Friday – Guest Speaker Meeting 
Saturday – AA Related Video Discussion
name: Isle of Misfits

description:
NEW WOMEN’S BIG BOOK STUDY STARTING APRIL 22, 2025: Come join this compassionate and inspired group of women as we study our textbook,
The Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous. It provides us with the instructions on how to proceed through the 12 Steps of recovery. We will begin on the inside cover and read through Dr. Bob’s Nightmare. We will read a paragraph or two at a time and then share our experience, strength and hope. Video must be on upon entering meeting.

Appropriate handouts will be provided.

Come to identify, learn, share, discuss, question, get a sponsor, do service, or just listen.

*This is a smaller meeting and a great place to learn and practice how to share, time, speaker share, host, security, etc…

A safe place for women who have the desire to not drink❣️
name: Sobriety Sisters Turning the Page

description:
Get to “The Point” of Recovery!

Strongly unified, we at Providence Point are held together by adherence to our Primary Purpose to carry the A.A. Message to the alcoholic who still suffers. We hope you will join us as an additional resource for your recovery.

We meet twice daily at 2 PM and 11 PM EST following a rotating format:

Monday: Big Book Study

Tuesday: As Bill Sees It

Wednesday: AA Grapevine

Thursday: Daily Reflections

Friday: Big Book Personal Stories 

Saturday/Sunday: Music and Sobriety

description:
This AA group is all about diving into the Big Book and the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions. 

We focus on reading, discussing, and sharing what this literature mean to us and how they guide our recovery. We dig deeper into the program, share our experiences, and learn from each other. 

Whether you’re new to AA or have been around for a while, everyone’s welcome. It’s all about connecting, growing, and staying grounded in the principles that help us live a sober and meaningful life.
name: Sunlight of the Spirit Book Study

description:
We meet on Sunday and Wednesday from 2 pm to 3:30 pm EST to dive deeply into the Big Book. We have some great Hosts who make the Big Book sing and come alive! Beginners and Old-timers are welcome! Come jumpstart your recovery and get our mind right. Come get armed with the facts about yourself and the AA program.  
Bring your Big Book, highlighter, pen and an Open Mind. Ask your  Sponsor and Sponsees to join in.

The Original Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020.

We have other workshops throughout the week! We have 18 meetings a day. We are open 24 hours on the weekends.
name: A Checkup From the Neck Up - Big Book Bootcamp!

description:
An International Young Peoples meeting of AA, open to ALL - young in age OR young at heart.
7 Days a week from 8 to 9 PM EST, followed by fellowship.
Nightly meeting format (all followed by open discussion):

Mon: As Bill Sees It.
Tues: 12 Steps & 12 Traditions.
Wed: Ask-It-Basket.
Thurs: Daily Reflection.
Fri: Grapevine.
Sat: Speaker.
Sun: Big Book Study.

Saturday Morning 10 AM EST Big Book Literature Study
Sunday Morning 10 AM EST Living Sober Literature Study

No passcode required, waiting room enabled.
Will provide meeting verification upon request."
name: A New Wave Young Peoples Group

description:
This meeting focuses on understanding AA’s 12 steps. We learn to stay sober by using the steps every day, one day at a time. Some old timers try to be like  beginners by reminding themselves of the AA basics every day. And old timers will tell you there is always something useful to learn from a meeting, even if you’ve been sober for decades.

We read and discuss AA literature.

You are welcome to ask questions about the reading or anything else about the AA program.
name: Beginners, Old-Timers, and Everyone Else

description:
The Essentials Group: an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous, meaning all are welcome regardless of whether they have a problem with alcoholism. We meet via Zoom every night of the week from 9:30PM-11:00PM PST

Essentials is a topic meeting; the chair will lead in sharing for 10 minutes, pick a topic, then call on people to share. The floor opens at 10:45pm, in which a share does not need to be on the night’s topic.

Wed nights (topic meeting) Birthday nights (last Friday of the month, speaker meeting), and 
Sat (speaker tape meeting) are hybrid meetings (Essentials at the Alano Club on the Eastside in Bellevue WA); 
all other nights are separate meetings (online separate from in-person)

The Essentials Group: an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous, meaning all are welcome regardless of whether they have a problem with alcoholism. We meet via Zoom every night of the week from 9:30PM-11:00PM PST

Essentials is a topic meeting; the chair will lead in sharing for 10 minutes, pick a topic, then call on people to share. The floor opens at 10:45pm, in which a share does not need to be on the night’s topic.

Wed nights (topic meeting) Birthday nights (last Friday of the month, speaker meeting), and 
Sat (speaker tape meeting) are hybrid meetings (Essentials at the Alano Club on the Eastside in Bellevue WA); 
all other nights are separate meetings (online separate from in-person)
name: The Essentials Group

description:
Sober Stogies is a closed, rather unconventional online discussion meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. We meet weekly on Wednesday at 11pm and Sunday at Noon - all times EST on zoom.
 
What makes us unconventional is our unanimous love for sobriety, spiritual progress and living in our common solution -- all while smoking fine cigars! If you're not a cigar lover, we hope you'll grab a seat in the non-smoking section and join us anyway. We of Sober Stogies are ALWAYS eager to share our experience, strength and hope with smokers and non-smokers alike!
name: Sober Stogies

description:
This AA group is all about diving into the Big Book and the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions. 

We focus on reading, discussing, and sharing what this literature mean to us and how they guide our recovery. We dig deeper into the program, share our experiences, and learn from each other. 

Whether you’re new to AA or have been around for a while, everyone’s welcome. It’s all about connecting, growing, and staying grounded in the principles that help us live a sober and meaningful life.

We come together in a safe and supportive environment to share our journeys and help one another stay sober. Whether you're new or have been here a while, there's a place for you in this circle.
Your presence and story matter.
name: Open Arms

description:
Unshakable Serenity is an open zoom meeting. We meet daily at 4 PM EST.

 Unshakable serenity refers to a state Unshakable Serenity" refers to a deep, unwavering state of inner peace and calm that remains steady no matter the chaos or challenges life throws your way. We have a strong commitment to the 12 Traditions and helping the next struggling alcoholic. 
Big Book Study on Saturdays. 
Topic discussions daily, chair’s choice. 
We welcome  newcomers and old timers alike! 
Please join us on the ride to serenity. Let us find our sober peace, without taking life too seriously!
name: Unshakable Serenity

description: Welcome! We're a fun and friendly group who takes our sobriety seriously. We read from the Daily Reflections and then open the meeting up for participation on either what was read or anything else as it relates to sobriety. Everyone is welcome and we can't wait to share a cup of coffee with you...on us!
name: Coffee Break 3:05 Pacific, 6:05 Eastern

description:
A Common Solution is a meeting that focuses on the 3 Legacies of Alcoholics Anonymous. 
Our format is a speaker meeting. The speaker will share on a topic given that relates to the program outlined in the first 164 pages of the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous.

We meet once a week. Tuesday’s at 8PM EST
name: A Common Solution

description:
This is an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. Together, we explore the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous—starting with the Foreword to the First Edition and continuing through A Vision for You. 

We believe the solution to our alcoholism lies within these pages, and we are committed to sharing that solution in each meeting.
Whether you have a Big Book or not, all are welcome. We display the readings on screen so everyone can follow along and join the discussion. Our goal is to provide a supportive and inclusive space for connection and recovery.
Newcomers and visitors are especially welcome. Come as you are.
We also do meeting verification,
name: Pathway to Serenity

description:
This was originally finally a fathers group but we changed it to “fatherhood focused”. 
This is a hybrid meeting Thursdays at 6pm EST at 85 Quincy Ave in Quincy, Massachusetts.
name: Burn The Boats

description: MOST is a closed men’s meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous, with a focus on Men Overcoming Sexual Trauma. MOST is safe environment where men are free to explore the role of sexual trauma in our addiction histories and to forge solutions optimum for our shared recovery.
name: The MOST AA Group

description:
Monday-Friday 1:00 PST

Newcomers welcome and verification sent upon request. 
Meeting closes at 10 minutes after the hour.
Discussion generated from AA approved literature. 
We are a relatively small group with new and varied times of sobriety. If you are looking for a home group that provides love, guidance, support, service work, and fellowship, come on in and join us. 
IN AN EFFORT TO KEEP OUR MEETING SAFE AND SECURE, WE ASK THAT YOU HAVE YOUR CAMERA ON UPON ENTERING.
Hope to see you soon as we trudge this happy road.

description:
We are a closed AA meeting for Women. 
We rotate Step, Discussion, Speaker, and Celebration Meetings during the month. 
Newcomers are Welcome and encouraged to share. Join us early for fellowship.
1st Saturday, Step meeting
2nd Saturday, Discussion
3rd Saturday, Speaker
4th Saturday, Celebration
name: This is Just For Today

description:
This meeting is set up to help members to learn and use the 12 steps of AA. 
We are a small group as of now, and we are determined to help support AA's growth here in Belize. 
This was originally a face to face meeting that morphed into a hybrid setting. Because Alcoholics Anonymous is not very well known to the Belizean majority, and because each District here is so far away from each other, the hope of this meeting is to bring this beautiful country together in our recovery,
as well as offering hope to those who need it. The format of the meeting is going through the 12 steps of AA and a speaker once monthly
name: What's The Point

name: Interview with an Alcoholic

description: Welcome to Sober Buddies — a faith-based recovery community where no one walks alone. We’re a safe space for those in recovery to grow spiritually, emotionally, and mentally. Rooted in Christ, we offer encouragement, accountability, and support through live meetings, motivational content, and real connection. Whether you’re just beginning or years into your journey, you belong here. We believe sobriety isn’t just about abstaining — it’s about becoming who God created you to be. Come as you are, and let’s walk this path of freedom together. You’re not alone — we are your Sober Buddies.
name: Sober Buddies United

description:
Come join our All Night Why Are You N.U.T.S? International Meeting!
N.U.T.S. is an acronym for Not Using The Steps.

We meet 7 days a week at 6:00 PM, 7:00 PM, 8:15 PM, 1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM, and 6:00 AM EST

Daily: 6:00 AM EST Daily Reflections (Mon - Fri)
Daily: 6:00 PM EST No Matter What Club! (Mon - Sun)
Daily: 7:00 PM EST Big Book Study (Mon - Sun)
Daily: 8:15 PM EST Joe & Charlie Tapes (Mon - Sun)

ROTATING FORMAT BELOW FOR OTHER HOURS

Monday: Steps 6 & 7 (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Tuesday: 12 x 12 Study (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Wednesday: Living Sober (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Thursday: As Bill Sees It (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Friday: Big Book Study (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM)
Sat/Sun: Music and Sobriety (1:00 AM, 2:30 AM, 4:30 AM, 6:00 AM)

All Inclusive!

If you are an alcoholic (or have a desire to stop drinking) You are Welcome here!

Doors Open Daily at Midnight (12 AM) EST!
name: All Night Why Are You N.U.T.S?

description:
The Liverpool Young Persons’ Meeting Online is a weekly online meeting which started in Liverpool, England, but welcomes fellows from around the world. While most of us first came into the fellowship when we were young, we welcome those of any age with a desire to stop drinking.

On the first Sunday of every month, we read the month’s corresponding step from 12 Steps and 12 Traditions. Our other meetings are speaker meetings, in which we have a main share followed by general sharing. 

The meeting runs from 7:30pm - 9:00 UK time, and we stay open for fellowship afterwards.
name: Liverpool Young Persons’ Meeting Online

description:
PNWF is a fellowship rooted firmly in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous and guided by the Twelve Traditions. This is a space where newcomers and old-timers alike can come together in unity, service, and recovery. 

Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety, just as outlined in the program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We read directly from the Big Book, share personal experience, strength, and hope, and keep our group grounded in the spiritual principles that have helped millions find freedom from alcoholism.

Though we meet online, we’re not just a digital group — we encourage members to connect locally as well.
name: Pacific Northwest Fellowship

description:
Terrapin Station is an open meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. We meet daily at 5PM PT. Come early, come late, whenever you arrive you’ll be right on time!
Every evening we have a different format with a variety of hosts and a Big Book study on Friday night. So, if your faced with mysteries dark and vast, can’t tell your pillow from a stone, if the life you're living’s no good and you’ve gone a little further than you’ve ever gone before, come get sober with us in the shadow of the moon in Terrapin! And remember friend, the ONLY requirement for AA membership is a desire to stop drinking. "Once in a while you get shown the light in the strangest of places if you look at it right."
name: Terrapin Station

description:
Our group of Alcoholics Anonymous is an open meeting that began during COVID as a splinter from a Bricks & Mortar group. We have since become independent and autonomous. We hold all of AA's Traditions closely to our hearts and minds. 
We firmly believe in carrying the message of AA to all those who suffer, both inside and outside the rooms of AA. 
We do not endorse, finance or lend the AA name to anything outside of our Group and its meetings. 
We are self-supporting through member donations for our Zoom channel alone. 
Please come and join our fun bunch! Room opens approximately 7:00 pm
Every Wednesday we have a volunteer Host(Chair)/Topic Leader (yes the same person) who shares some Experience, Strength and Hope on a Topic of their choice; barring any newcomer or sobriety-threatening issues. 
Anyone who would like to become a regular attendee can be added to the shared Google sheet and volunteer their service to Host/Topic Lead. We have no requirement for length of sobriety to do so.
Please come and join our fun bunch! Room opens approximately 7:00 pm
name: New Freedom Topic Lead

description:

We may be the new kids on the block, but we’re already making some noise — the *sober* kind, of course! Our group is just getting started, and we’re thrilled to be a part of the fellowship and to grow with your support. 
Our first (and currently only) meeting is the **Sober Sounds Music Meeting**, where recovery meets rhythm. Whether you're into jazz, punk, country, or just good ol' acoustic honesty, come share, listen, and find connection through music and experience, strength, and hope. 
🎤 **Service opportunities available** — if you’ve got a desire to stay sober and a willingness to help, we’ve got a place for you!**

description:
Welcome to The Isle of Misfits!  We are inclusive, never exclusive – ALL are welcome!  Our meetings are a mixture of book studies and open/topic discussions.  We like to take the time to really break the down readings and ask questions, so we truly understand the literature.  We also seek to understand the reasons behind our behaviors and more importantly to find solutions!   
We meet on M-Sat at 12PM EST and Monday night at 7PMEST.   
Monday – Big Book Study 
Monday PM (7pm EST) – Big Book Study – Personal Stories from the back of the book  
Tuesday – Topic Discussion 
Wednesday – Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions Study 
Thursday – AA Related Book Study  
Friday – Guest Speaker Meeting 
Saturday – AA Related Video Discussion
name: Isle of Misfits

description:
PNWF is a fellowship rooted firmly in the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous and guided by the Twelve Traditions. This is a space where newcomers and old-timers alike can come together in unity, service, and recovery. 

Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics achieve sobriety, just as outlined in the program of Alcoholics Anonymous. We read directly from the Big Book, share personal experience, strength, and hope, and keep our group grounded in the spiritual principles that have helped millions find freedom from alcoholism.

Though we meet online, we’re not just a digital group — we encourage members to connect locally as well.
name: Pacific Northwest Fellowship

description:

We gather to share experience, strength and hope, carrying forward the principles of Alcoholics Anonymous with a focus on growth, compassion and accountability. Our name reflects the truth many of us know we have stood on the edge before, but together we find a way back into life, into fellowship and into recovery.

MONDAY

FRIDAY
• Speaker — 8pm PST / 11pm EST
• Topics — 9pm PST / Midnight EST
• 12 & 12 — 10pm PST / 1am EST
SATURDAY
• Speaker — 8pm PST / 11pm EST
• Topics — 9pm PST / 12am EST
*Big Book Study 10pm PST / 1am EST

description:
This is a Gratitude AA meeting focused on sharing the gifts of recovery. We begin with a reading of Chapter 5 from the Big Book, followed by open sharing. Members raise their hands and are given 2–3
minutes to speak on what they’re grateful for that day, what they’re thankful for in life, and how recovery has shown up for them. After the initial round of sharing, we observe the 7th Tradition and read the 12 Steps. We then return to open sharing, continuing the spirit of gratitude and connection. This meeting is a space to reflect, celebrate recovery, and honor the daily blessings of sobriety.
name: The 22:22 Gratitude meeting of AA International

description:
Join us for ANYTHING GOES, a unique and engaging Alcoholics Anonymous history meeting where our resident AA historian, Thom R., takes us down the rabbit hole into the rich, strange, and often surprising archives of AA’s past - from long-forgotten stories and buried records to mysterious events, lesser-known figures, and the evolution of AA’s principles and practices. Expect rare documents,  curious trivia, historical insights, and lively discussion. No topic is off limits - if it's part of AA's history, it’s fair game. 

Whether you're a history buff, a curious newcomer, or just looking for something a little different in your weekly meeting, ANYTHING GOES offers a fascinating journey.
name: The 10:10 Group: ANYTHING GOES AA History Meeting

description:
Video apagado. Micrófono, se prende solamente para compartir y las oraciones.. 
Apuntamos ntro nombre en chat al ingresar para respetar Tradición XII y compartimos en el orden que nos apuntamos.
Somos un grupo tradicional de Propósito Primordial. Nuestra reunión se basa en la solución . Se realiza en español. La duración es de una hora y media. Comenzamos con la Oración de la Serenidad y concluimos con el Padre Nuestro. Elegimos un tema diario basado en las Reflexiones y leemos literatura aprobada por AA entre cada compartimiento.

Martes: - Libro Grande
Miércoles: - 12 y 12
Jueves: - El Lenguaje del Corazón
Viernes: Fany - Llegamos a creer
Sábado: Yolis - Libro Grande
Domingo: - Como lo ve Bill

description: Our Workshops began September 2021, meeting weekly on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Tuesday's Workshop (5-6:15 PM PT) was created to deepen our experience with the simple solution to alcoholism laid out in the Big Book and the 12 &12. We read through the Big Book until we finish a step, then read the essay on the same Step in the 12&12 in the same way, pausing for questions or comments after each paragraph. Our Wednesday Traditions and History Workshop (5:45-7 PM PT) was created to discover and deepen our understanding of the circumstances experienced by our early members, as purposefully recorded by one of our founders. Our historical exploration utilizes AA conference approved literature. All are welcome to attend.
name: Shoulder to Shoulder Online Group

description: Welcome to Sober Buddies — a faith-based recovery community where no one walks alone. We’re a safe space for those in recovery to grow spiritually, emotionally, and mentally. Rooted in Christ, we offer encouragement, accountability, and support through live meetings, motivational content, and real connection. Whether you’re just beginning or years into your journey, you belong here. We believe sobriety isn’t just about abstaining — it’s about becoming who God created you to be. Come as you are, and let’s walk this path of freedom together. You’re not alone — we are your Sober Buddies.
name: Sober Buddies United

description:
Tradition Five states: Each group has but one primary purpose — to carry its message to the alcoholic who still suffers. 
The short form of Tradition One states: “Our common welfare should come first; personal recovery depends upon A.A. unity.” Recognizing the importance of group unity, our group strives to create a safe meeting environment in which alcoholics can focus on achieving sobriety. 
Our primary purpose is to carry the message of recovery Alcoholics Anonymous to those still suffering from alcoholism.
name: Emotional Sobriety in AA - Emotional Sobriety

description:
A Sober Beginning is an open AA meeting focused on helping newcomers leap into action implementing the solution to their problems with alcohol as described in the first 164 pages of the Big Book.   

Our meeting is focused on the solution rather than the problem. We encourage constructive feedback. 

We ask that attendees are attentive, respectful and treat our meeting as they would work or school.  If you can’t quit completely, can’t control your drinking, and feel miserable when you stop — we have a solution.
name: A Sober Beginning – A beginners meeting for MEN

description:
This meeting is for us in recovery to gather with our fellows in a morning meditative yoga practice where we attempt to connect our mind, body, and spirit, so we may become more mindful of the 24 hours ahead. We encourage all participants to do with this time as they wish, asking that all attendees keep their video off and mic muted for the duration of the yoga practice to ensure no distractions during the meeting. The purpose of this meeting is to help people achieve
recovery by the daily practice of movement and meditation with the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous as our guide. We share our experience, strength and hope with each other that we may solve our common problem  and help others to recover from their alcoholism.

Friday is a Guided Meditation in place or Yoga, followed by an A.A. meeting.

description:
Back from the Edge 2.0 is an open AA meeting built on renewal, honesty and connection. We gather to share experience, strength and hope, carrying forward the principles of Alcoholics Anonymous with a focus on growth, compassion and accountability. Our name reflects the truth many of us know we have stood on the edge before, but together we find a way back into life, into fellowship and into recovery.

SUNDAY
• Plain Language Big Book — 8pm PST / 11pm EST
MONDAY
• Daily Reflections — 8pm PST / 11pm EST
FRIDAY
• Speaker — 8pm PST / 11pm EST
• Topics — 9pm PST / Midnight EST
• 12 & 12 — 10pm PST / 1am EST
SATURDAY
• Speaker — 8pm PST / 11pm EST
• Topics — 9pm PST / 12am EST
*Big Book Study 10pm PST / 1am EST

We now offer Proof of Attendance, we offer this service to people needing it for courts, employment or whatever is needed for verification.

description: We are a group of folks who not only suffer from alcoholism but who are also afflicted with various conditions that cause us chronic pain. We have come together to support the pursuit of healthy living for ourselves and others while we apply the art of living sober and manage our chronic pain. Our meeting takes place on Tuesday evening at 8 pm. It is a closed discussion meeting with a speaker in place on the last Tuesday of the month.5 All are welcome to join with us in fellowship and conversation as we find ways to Live Sober with Chronic Pain.
name: Living Sober with Chronic Pain

description:
Sober Patrol is a closed men’s veterans Alcoholics Anonymous meeting for those with a desire to stop drinking who seek camaraderie, discipline, and mutual support. We begin with the Promises and a daily affirmation. The meeting leader speaks for up to ten minutes and sets the topic, then calls on members for three-minute shares. Seventh
Tradition is observed at the 30-minute mark. We close with the Lord’s Prayer. All veterans identifying as alcoholic are welcome.
name: Veterans Sober Patrol

description:
Ever been surprised by an Advisory Action, only to find out the US/CAN General Service Conference has been discussing it for 6 or 7 years?
This won’t happen again if you attend our Final Conference Report reviews where Conference members present topics they participated in during the most recent General Service Conference and answer your questions.  
Each weekly meeting focuses on the Final Conference Report starting with its release (usually in early September) until we’re done (usually at the end of January). We read related Conference-approved literature in the off-season. In 2026, we’ll be returning to Our Great Responsibility, a collection of Bill W.’s talks and essays.
Please join us!
name: Final Conference Report Review

description: Our open Monday Meditation meeting  includes a spiritual reading related to the 12 steps along with a lead, followed by a 20 minute guided meditation and time for comments/sharing. We focus on the 12th Step and inclusive spirituality.
name: Monday Meditation

description: A step 11-based meeting, we review a selection of spiritual content weekly followed by a 10 minute meditation then sharing. Content changes monthly, and we encourage use of pen and paper to record thoughts and ideas that come during meditation. Our goal is to improve our conscious contact with our Higher Power in all forms. All are welcome!
name: Spiritual Conditioning

description: We focus on reading from the Big Book of AA on the eleventh step, a 5 minute guided meditation to begin, a brief lead, then comment/sharing. The focus is on improving our conscious contact with a god of our understanding, and praying for the knowledge of god's will for us and the power to carry it out. We end with an optional 15 minute guided meditation from 8 -8:15
name: 11@7 Meditation Meeting

description:

Being young is a state of mind!

We have various topic discussions each day. People of any age can join. This is a co-ed meeting.

We have over 20 meetings everyday and recovery workshops.

The Zoo Crew has been on Zoom since March of 2020. We have picnics around the country for meet and greets. Come join our international community.

description:
This virtual group started on Friday, March 13, 2020 as a result of COVID shutdown by 12 close LGBT+ & Straight Sober friends & fellows from around the globe. The only requirement for AA membership is a desire to stop drinking! The only requirement to join this meeting is active participation in our continuous review and practical application of the 12 Steps found in our basic text and the first 164 Pages of the Big Book. Meetings are 7 days a week – Same Time – Same Meeting Link – Different Format Every Day:
Sunday - Prayer & Meditation
Monday - Wheel of Sobriety
Tuesday - Cross Talk
Wednesday - As Bill Sees It
Thursday - The Long Haul
Friday - Random / Random
Saturday - Week in Review
name: You Are The Company You Keep

description:
Sober Knights is an open meeting for gentlemen who wish to share their experience, strength and hope in sobriety. 
We meet nightly at 8:15 pm Eastern Time and have topic and discussion meetings. 

Our format is as follows:

Monday - Newcomers Meeting
Tuesday - 12 & 12 (Last Tuesday of the month is a Traditions Meeting).
Wednesday , Friday - Topic followed by open shares.
Thursday -  "As Bill Sees It" followed by open shares.
Saturday - Topic and Share on first and third Saturdays of the month, AA Q&A second Sat, and Speaker meeting last Saturday.
Sunday - Big Book Study

Unicorn Horns & Pixie Dust is not a glum lot!  We are a welcoming group where newcomers are always encouraged and supported! If you have a desire to stop drinking, you are welcome here! Our meetings offer a safe, respectful and fun space to listen, share, and connect with others on the path of recovery!

All meetings are closed AA meetings, except our Tuesday Speaker Meeting, which is open to all. Attendance verification is available!

All meeting times are in Central Time.

Monday 10PM: Dual Diagnosis 
Tuesday 10PM: Speaker Meeting (Open)
Wednesday 12AM: Topic Discussion
Wednesday 10PM: Topic Discussion
Thursday 10PM: Music Meeting
Friday 10PM: Ask It Basket 
Saturday 10PM: Game Night

Everyone is welcome to attend this meeting. Is an Open Meeting.

Our Focus is on the solution for recovery from alcoholism.
If you are looking for a new home group you just found it, join us.
We are always looking for new service members as well to help with the meeting.
Love to hear from Newcomers. Love to hear how you are staying sober.
We do send a verification for attending our meeting.

We Fellowship Before and After the meeting as well.

19th Street Group operates out of Harrisburg, PA. The group hosts 4 Zoom meetings a week; format is a reading from the AA approved literature in the meeting’s title, followed by a discussion of what was read. We have a "Parking Lot" time for up to 30 minutes after the meeting for fellowship. Please join us!

No passcode required; waiting room enabled and all attendees are muted upon entering.

19th Street Group’s online meetings are:

Sundays at 7:00, Big Book
Tuesdays at 7:00, Came To Believe/Living Sober
Thursdays at 7:00, 12 x 12 (Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions)
Fridays at 8:30, Daily Reflections

The group hosts 4 Zoom meetings a week; format is a reading from the AA approved literature in the meeting’s title, followed by a discussion of what was read. We have a "Parking Lot" time for up to 30 minutes after the meeting for fellowship. Please join us!

No passcode required; waiting room enabled and all attendees are muted upon entering.

19th Street Group’s online meetings are:

Sundays at 7:00, Big Book
Tuesdays at 7:00, Came To Believe/Living Sober
Thursdays at 7:00, 12 x 12 (Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions)
Fridays at 8:30, Daily Reflections
name: 19th Street Online - Living Sober / Came to Believe

description:
We welcome you to join us in a safe and loving environment where we focus on recovery from alcoholism. You will meet people counting days as well as those with years of sobriety. Newcomers are welcome and encouraged to share and get active in AA.  Please join our closed meeting, open to anyone who has a desire to stop drinking.  We meet seven (7) days a week at 5 PM Eastern Time.
We do send email meeting verification for attending.
Monday: Lead share on As Bill Sees It
Tuesday: Lead share on a Daily Reflections
Wednesday: We discuss the Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions
Thursday: We discuss the Third Step
Friday: Lead share on Topic
Saturday: We discuss the Big Book 
Sunday: We have a speaker meeting. The speaker has 40 minutes.

We hold an anniversary meeting on the last weekday of every month. Shares on how you’re staying sober.
We hold a group conscience meeting on the first Monday of every month  following our regular meeting starting at 6:10 PM (Eastern Time).

name: Wednesday 5:00 Women’s Closed Big Book

description:
Every night at one minute before Midnight (PST), a “closed” gut-level discussion, AA meeting. If you have problems as they relate to alcoholism, come join us on Zoom, 7 nights a week!

The Midnight Howlers Group of Alcoholics Anonymous adheres to the Twelve Traditions. We maintain only the least amount of organization possible.

We ask that you support & respect others in the meeting. We look forward to meeting you as we zoom the road of happy destiny!

description:
Welcome all alcoholics—newcomers, old-timers and those in-between. Our literature-based discussion meeting focuses on AA's singleness of purpose: recovery from alcoholism. We look forward to seeing you and sharing with you!

No password is needed to join this meeting. You will enter a waiting room, and the chairperson will admit you.

Monday - Daily Reflections
Tuesday - Literature Based Topic (Open Discussion)
Wednesday - Chairperson’s Choice
Thursday - Big Book Study (We'll read a few paragraphs out of the Big Book and open the floor for discussion
name: A New Start

description:
It's a hybrid AA meeting of in person and Zoom going on at the same time.  
We at BYOBB (Bring Your Own Big Book) are a group of alcoholics dedicated to following the program of Alcoholics Anonymous outlined in the Big Book. 
We have a speaker read a bit from the Big Book and then speak on what he or she read – that then sets the subject for the discussion for the remainder of the meeting.
name: BYOBB

GRUPO HIMALAYA ZOOM

Grupo de A.A. tradicional de habla hispana, sesionamos de Lunes a Viernes de 8 pm a 9:30 pm hora del centro de México. Durante las reuniones nos apoyamos con literatura de A. A. y compartimos experiencia, fortaleza y esperanza.

Autonomía durante las reuniones: 
Mantener micrófonos en silencio mientras no se está compartiendo.
Tratar de mantener cámaras encendidas.
Respetar la catarsis de los demás.
No entrar en controversias ni hacer señalamientos a ningún compañero.
Tiempo máximo de compartimiento 10 minutos.

description: This meeting is meant for those struggling with alcoholism and addiction. This is a closed meeting solely for Law enforcement, firefighters, military, and corrections. All active duty and retired members are welcome. No access to this meeting will be permitted without the password and live video. (Sorry, no phone calls or email access). This meeting focuses on recovery for struggling alcoholics trying to stay sober. Anonymity is highly required. All local, state, and federal personnel are welcome. This meeting is new and hopefully we can talk about our disease and daily work struggles in confidence. This is an open forum. 12 steps, serenity prayer, and the lords prayer will be introduced in each meeting. No civilians please.
name: First Responders AA MEETING

description:
We are a small but welcoming Frankfurt-based group of Alcoholics Anonymous for LGBT+ Allies  in recovery. 
Alcoholics Anonymous is a fellowship of men and women who share their experience, strength and hope with each other that they may solve their common problem and help others to recover from alcoholism. The only requirement for membership is a desire to stop drinking. There are no dues or fees for A.A. membership; we are self-supporting through our own contributions. A.A. is not allied with any sect, denominations, politics, organization or institution; does not wish to engage in any controversy, neither endorses nor opposes any causes. Our primary purpose is to stay sober and help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety.
name: Live and Let Live Frankfurt International LGBTQI+

description: BYOBB is a welcoming and interactive Big Book study group that meets every Monday at 6pm pacific standard zone on Zoom. Our purpose is to develop a deeper understanding of the Alcoholics Anonymous Big Book and how its principles apply to our daily lives. We take time to explore the text in small sections, often using a dictionary from the time the Big Book was written to better understand key terms and ideas. Through open sharing and real-life experience, we connect the message of recovery to personal growth and healing. Whether you’re new to the program or have been around for a while, this group offers a thoughtful and supportive space to grow in recovery, one paragraph at a time.

description:
Do you have a desire to stop drinking? If yes, you are in the right place.



Are you ready to take all 12 Steps of Alcoholics Anonymous?



"If you want what we have and are willing to go to any lengths to get it, then you are ready to take certain steps." AA



We'll follow instructions in the AA Big Book taking ALL 12 steps in one sitting. (w/coffee breaks and lunch of course)



IF YOU CAN'T STAY THE ENTIRE 6 HOURS, DON'T BOTHER COMING. (Sometimes goes a little bit longer.) NO ONE WILL BE ADMITTED AFTER 1:00 PM EST.



This workshop usually has from 1 - 3 people in it, which helps everyone to focus.

description:
We are the Women’s Early Risers Group of Alcoholics Anonymous. We are a closed meeting, except on Saturdays and the 4th Sunday of the Month when we celebrate Anniversaries we are an OPEN meeting.

Monday: Big Book Study
Tuesday: Daily Reflections begins with 5 minute silent meditation 
Wednesday: Chair's Choice: The chairperson will choose an AA approved topic for today's meeting.
Thursday: Beginners meeting discussion. After speaker, the shares start in this order: 
0-30 days sobriety | 31-60 days sobriety | 61-90 days sobriety
91-6 months sobriety | 6 -9 months sobriety | less than one year | 
Anyone can share.
Friday: Step Series
Saturday: Speaker Discussion (OPEN Meeting)
Sunday: Book series

* We celebrate Anniversaries on the 4th Sunday of the month. Anniversary Celebrations are also OPEN Meetings
No passcode required.
name: Women’s Early Risers

description:
This daily meeting was started by members of the Southside Group in Tucson, AZ who moved away, but wanted to stay connected and continue to carry the message of sobriety to newcomers nationwide. We strongly recommend sponsorship, meetings, and working the 12 steps. We love AA and are grateful for sobriety.

Each night we also have a "Meeting after the meeting", where we invite newcomers to ask questions and get phone numbers and maybe get a sponsor, and it also provides fellowship for all members. *NEWCOMERS ENCOURAGED TO ATTEND*

The Attitude Adjustment Group provides a virtual A.A meeting room every Mon-Sat at 7:30am CST for us to come together and safely share our experience, strength and hope with one another so that we may stay sober and help other alcoholics to achieve sobriety. 
If you have a desire to stop drinking, you are very welcome to join us!

Our daily meeting formats: 
 - Monday: Speaker's Choice (AA Literature) discussion

 - Friday: Grapevine discussion
 - Saturday: Big Book Study

description:
Part of the 1 Day at a Time Online Group of Alcoholics Anonymous

We read small sections of the book Alcoholics Anonymous (Big Book) and then open the meeting to group discussion on the weekly topic. 

Closed meeting. Attendance at closed meetings is limited to persons who have a desire to stop drinking. If you think you have a problem with alcohol, you are welcome to attend this meeting.

We abide by the 12 Traditions and ask attendees to not take screenshots or recordings of any kind. We do not sign court slips or offer proof of attendance. 

Free online copies of the book “Alcoholics Anonymous” (the Big Book) can be found here: https://www.aa.org/pages/en_US/alcoholics-anonymous
name: Big Book (1DAAT)

description:
The Recovering Righteous Rebellion was created as an initiative of a greater vision to do the following:

Inspire humans to lead meaningful lives through AA 12 Steps.
To impact the world through outreach and AA fellowship.
Help shape the AA fellowship of tomorrow through spreading the unapologetic message of being sober and genuinely being and embracing your authentic self.

We meet 7 days a week:
Mindful Monday
Traditions Tuesday
Wandering Wednesday
Therapeutic Thursday
Friendly Friday
Step Study Saturday
Sober Sundays All Kind Humans

No perfect humans allowed. No exceptions.
name: The Recovering Righteous Rebellion

description:
Closed meeting for AA members, for those who have a desire to stop drinking or who believe they have a drinking problem.
Format: Multi-format
1st Week Discussion of any one (1), two (2) or three (3) consecutive paragraphs from the “Big Book”.
2nd Week Discussion of any topic directly related to the writing in the “Big Book” with which the speaker is familiar.
3rd Week Discussion of any one (1), two (2) or three (3) consecutive paragraphs from the “Big Book”
4th Week Step meeting – Discussion of Step as contained in the “Big Book”. Speaker is to discuss only those steps he/she has completed or is currently working through the 12 Step process.
5th Week For months with a fifth Wednesday in them a discussion of any topic directly related.

Closed AA Meeting. LGBTQIA+, Neurodivergent, and Dual Diagnosis friendly.

Rotating Format:
Speaker - 20-40 minute share speaker picks a topic and open up for shares.
Literature - A passage is read and expanded on by a fellow AA member then opened up for shares.
Topic/Discussion - List of topic related to sobriety, tools of AA, the program and your recovery to share Experience Strength and Hope on.

description:
Closed AA Women's Meeting

Join us weekly for a rotating format:
- Speaker - 20-40 minute share, speaker picks topic open it up for discussion
- Literature - A passage read then broke down by a fellow AA member then opened up for discussion
- Topic/Discussion - List of Topic questions pertaining to the program, your recovery, sobriety, and staying and living sober to share your Experience Strength and Hope on.

We celebrate with chips and cake come celebrate you day or year count with us!

description:
Интернациональная группа АА «ИГрАА» проводится ежедневно, в конференц-программе ZOOM, в видеоформате, на русском языке.
АА «ИГрАА» проводит ежедневные закрытые собрания для алкоголиков.

Группа представлена участниками примерно из 20-ти стран Мира, географический охват постоянно раширяется. Благодаря видеосвязи атмосфера на группе приближена к живой встрече.

Начало проведения собрания (ежедневно):
9 a.m. New York Time/USA
15.00 Central European Time
17:00 Москва/Россия

Официальная часть собрания 1 час 30 минут, затем неофициальная часть в формате свободного общения для новых и постоянных участников группы.

Пн., вт., ср., чт, сб.: чтение отрыка книги «Анонимные Алкоголики», «12 шагов 12 традиций», обсуждение по прочитанному и возможность задать дополнительные темы, которые касаются АА и алкоголизма.
Пт и Вс.: спикерские собрания с возможностью задать вопрос спикеру. Иностранным спикерам обеспечивается синхронный перевод на русский
язык.

description:
"Once a cucumber becomes a pickle, it can never be a cucumber again!

Proud Pickles gather 7 days a week, 11 am EST and @ 8 pm EST

Meeting formats will vary from Host to Host. Still, they will include Big Book Studies, Daily Reflections, Inspirational Stories, readings from Women in Recovery, and anything else our pickled minds can come up with. We pickles like to color outside the jar!

The opposite of addiction is connection, and with the singleness of purpose in mind, we hope to build a community where all women in recovery feel safe, loved, and supported. We don't do this alone!

Check out our website for meeting access, resources, and a private community page.

Monday - The Promises

Thursday- Newcomer and main share
Friday- Spin the wheel and topic share 
Saturday- Stories from the Big Book experience strength and hope

First Sunday of every month Women's meditation meeting, Last Sunday of every month Men's meeting - email for details. 

Together we are stronger.

description:
Shoulder to Shoulder is a closed meeting of Alcoholics Anonymous. All who have a desire to stop drinking are welcome to join us. We meet online every Sunday at 9:00am ET to study the text of the Big Book of Alcoholics Anonymous to get a better understanding of the ideas, principles and steps of AA. We also like to enjoy ourselves while we do this and, if
we are blessed, make a friend or two!
We read paragraph by paragraph and participants can come in at any time to share. We encourage cross talk which fosters a friendly and emotionally connected meeting. We offer fellowship with understanding, support and humor. AND, free verification of attendance.
Newcomers and Oldtimers alike are welcome!
name: Shoulder to Shoulder

description:
Grupo tradicional de estudio con la mision de proporcionar un espacio seguro y acogedor donde las personas que luchan contra el alcoholismo puedan encontrar apoyo, comprension y las herramientas necesarias para una vida sobria.

Reuniones Diarias de 7:30 a 9:00 PM | CST - Tiempo del Centro de Mexico

Lunes : Libro Grande
Martes : Llegamos a Creer
Miercoles : Lenguaje del Corazon
Jueves : Tal Como la Ve Bill
Viernes : 12 Pasos
Sabado : Viviendo Sobrio
Domingo : Tradiciones

Formato usual de las reuniones : Lectura breve + Compartimiento 5-10 min por persona (a juicio del coordinador). No exceso de lenguaje soez ni comportamiento disruptivo.

No importa dónde te encuentres, estamos aquí para apoyarte.
name: Viveros Virtual MX

MONDAY 19.30 UK - Speaker Topic Meeting 90 mins, 35 min speaker chair followed by share-backs

description:
During this meeting, we read a full or portion of a chapter or personal story from the book Alcoholics Anonymous. We then discuss the reading one at a time. Participation in reading and discussing is optional. Those who wish to listen are welcome.
This meeting covers the main body of the book (doctor's opinion & 164 pages) then one part of the stories (parts 1, 2 or 3) before restarting at the beginning of the book.
This is a closed meeting so anyone who feels they may have a problem with alcohol is welcome. 
Attendance is normally less than 10.

description:
We are so glad you are here! Connection is the opposite of addiction, and you never have to do this alone again. 

We are an AA group that uses the 12 steps and traditions to help us navigate life in recovery and Live in the Solution together. This Chicago-based group originated during the Pandemic and has been going strong since.

We meet daily at 7:30AM CST to discuss recovery and emotional sobriety. We share our experience, strength, and hope with each other to help each other stay sober through life's ups and downs.

Monday-Thursday: Topic & Discussion
Friday: 1st Step Lead & Discussion
Saturday: Big Book Lead & Discussion
Sunday: 12 & 12 Lead & Discussion
name: Living in the Solution

description:
This is a closed meeting for alcoholics or people who have a desire to stop drinking. We have three meetings which is determined by the chair person. We have a big book meeting, where we will read a page or two from the big book then open it up for discussion. A topic meeting, where we get 4-5 topics from attendees to be discussed during the meeting. With the lead share meeting, a speaker will share for about 20-25 minutes then we will open up the room for discussion. Please keep anything AA related with you. It may be needed to show your are involved with AA and help prevent zoom disrupters from being unmuted.

description: We read the doctor's opinion through to the stories after the first 164 pages, and then start over again. We read for approximately 20 minutes and then open the meeting to raised hand sharing on the topic of what has been read or anything an attendee wishes to share. We have been doing this for the past five years. Many of us have been trudging buddies for more than forty years. This is a closed meeting. All with a desire to stop drinking are welcome.
name: As Outlined in the Big Book

description:
This meeting is safe place for members of AA and other recovery backgrounds to meet and discuss our journeys in recovery. ALL ARE WELCOME! 
This is an open meeting and all are welcomed! Please remember this is a safe space for those in recovery, but also a space for those in the LGBTQIA community to meet and support each other! No bullying, no drama, no racial slurs, no discriminatory comments will be tolerated or allowed. 
Topics: We will read texts from the Book Alcoholics Anonymous, Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions, As Bill Sees It, and The Daily Reflections. 
Meeting days will be as follows:
Wednesday at 8 pm EST
Saturday at 8 am EST
In the future we hope to all hold speaker meetings as the group grows!
name: LGBTQIA AA and Recovery meeting

We meet 7 days a week at 12:00 pm & 10:30 pm EST. Beginners and old-timers are Welcome! Sobriety is not boring. Get your mind right!
Being young is a state of mind! 

We have various topic discussions each day. Women of any age can join.
We have over 20 meetings everyday and recovery workshops.

community.

description:
We meet every day to stay sober and to facilitate the daily maintenance of our spiritual condition.

Please join us at 6:00 AM (U.S. Pacific)/ 9:00 AM (U.S. Eastern).

Monday Beginner Meeting - we invite a member of AA to share for 15 minutes on Step 1, 2, or 3 (rotation)

Tuesday Topic Meeting – we discuss topics suggested by our members

Wednesday Speaker Meeting – we invite a member of our homegroup to share their story for 15-30 minutes, followed by a sharing session

Thursday Big Book Meeting – we read and discuss pages xxv - 164 of the book Alcoholics Anonymous

Friday As Bill Sees It Meeting – we read and discuss sections from the book As Bill Sees It: The A.A. Way of Life

Saturday Step/Tradition Meeting – we read and discuss the AA book Twelve Steps and Twelve Traditions

Sunday Speaker Meeting – we invite a member of AA to share their story for 30-45 minutes

Sunday Anniversary Meeting (the last Sunday of the month) – we celebrate sober anniversaries

description:
Join us 7 days a week for a fresh start and honest connection. 9:00 PM EST | 6:00 PM PST

This is a beginner-friendly meeting where all are welcome. If you have the desire to stop drinking, you are welcome here - no matter where you are in your journey.

description:
Focus on the Solution from Alcoholism.

Everyone is welcome to attend, especially Newcomers.

This is an Online / Zoom meeting following the traditions and principles of Alcoholics Anonymous.

Our group's meetings are AA Topic Lead share. Lead share for up to 10 minutes.

On the first Friday of every month is a tradition study. The tradition study is the tradition of the month that we are in.

Meeting from the Oregon Coast.. We are International on Zoom.

We do send attendance verification for attending.

Group Conscience Business meeting is Last Saturday following the regular meeting.

We need your help with our meeting! If you are looking for some service to do join us.

We are always looking for Home Group Members!
